definition_en: for the greatest part of a group or amount; in most cases or most of the time; and almost entirely

senses.title: The greatest share of a group
senses.definition: applying to the greater number of people or things in a group
senses.definitionCN: 适用于一个群体中数量占多数的人或物
senses.example: The guests at the wedding were mostly relatives from her side.
senses.exampleCN: 婚礼上的宾客多半是她这边的亲戚。
senses.why: The word is built on the Old English superlative māst, the greatest share, so its first duty is to report how a whole divides rather than to name a frequency.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在古英语最高级 māst（最大的份额）上，所以它首先管的是「一个整体怎么分」，而不是说事情多久发生一次。

senses.title: In most cases, as a habit
senses.definition: happening on most occasions, though not on every one
senses.definitionCN: 在多数场合都会发生，但并非每一次
senses.example: He mostly takes the early train and reads on the way.
senses.exampleCN: 他通常坐早班车，在路上看书。
senses.why: Once the word could mark the larger part of anything, it could also mark the larger part of a routine, which is how a share of a group turned into a habitual frequency.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词能标出任何事物里较大的那部分，它也就能标出日常习惯里较大的那部分，群体份额就这样长成了习惯性的频率。

senses.title: Nearly the whole of an amount
senses.definition: covering the largest part of a quantity or substance, with only a small remainder
senses.definitionCN: 占去数量或物质的最大部分，只剩下很少一点
senses.example: The bottle in the shed is mostly rainwater.
senses.exampleCN: 棚子里那瓶装的几乎全是雨水。
senses.why: Measuring a substance leaves a visible remainder, so the same superlative sense reads as a near total: the greatest share of a bottle is almost the bottle, and the rest is an exception.
senses.whyCN: 给一样东西计量时总会剩下一小点，于是同一个最高级的意思读成了「接近全部」：一只瓶子里的最大份额就是几乎整瓶，剩下那点只是例外。

intro.en: Mostly is an Old English superlative turned into an adverb: most, the greatest share, plus the ending -ly, which says in what manner a statement holds.
intro.cn: mostly 是古英语最高级加副词词尾构成的词：most 指最大的份额，-ly 表示一句话以什么方式成立。

items.en: Māst was the superlative of micel, great, and it named the greatest amount or the greatest share of a group.
items.cn: māst 是 micel（大的）的最高级，指最大的数量，或一个群体中最大的份额。

items.en: The ending -līce came from līc, body or form, and it turned an adjective into an adverb meaning in the manner of something; in English it settled as -ly.
items.cn: -līce 这个词尾出自 līc（身体、形貌），把形容词变成表示「以……方式」的副词；进入英语后固定为 -ly。

items.en: Middle English joined most and -ly into mostli, an adverb reporting what holds for the greater number of cases.
items.cn: 中古英语把 most 与 -ly 合成 mostli，用作副词，表示对多数情形都成立。

items.en: By the fifteenth century mostly was common in the sense of for the greatest part, and it stood beside almost, which had grown from all and most.
items.cn: 到十五世纪，mostly 已常见，意为「大部分」；它与由 all 与 most 合成的 almost 并列使用。

items.en: Modern English keeps three readings: a share of a group, a habitual frequency, and a near total in amount, and dictionaries list them as separate senses.
items.cn: 现代英语保留三种读法：群体中的份额、习惯性的频率、数量上接近全部；词典把它们分列为不同义项。

normalIntro.en: The word is one Old English superlative plus one adverbial ending, and everything about it follows from the idea of the greatest share.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是一个古英语最高级加一个副词词尾，它的全部用法都从「最大份额」这个想法里长出来。

normal.en: Most is the superlative of great, so mostly begins with the idea of the greatest share, not with a vague idea of many.
normal.cn: most 是 great 的最高级，所以 mostly 的起点是「最大份额」，而不是笼统的「很多」。

normal.en: -ly comes from an Old English word for body or form, and it turns an adjective into a statement about manner.
normal.cn: -ly 出自古英语里表示身体或形貌的词，它把形容词变成说明「方式」的词。

normal.en: Almost is all plus most, a near total, and it sits beside mostly in the same family of degree words.
normal.cn: almost 是 all 加 most，表示接近全部，它与 mostly 并排站在同一族程度词里。

normal.en: Weather reports say mostly sunny because the forecast covers most of a region and most of a day, not every square metre or every minute.
normal.cn: 天气预报说 mostly sunny，因为预报覆盖的是一个地区的大部分和一天的大部分，而不是每一平方米、每一分钟。

normal.en: Mostly because names the leading reason among several, which is the same share logic applied to causes instead of things.
normal.cn: mostly because 指几个原因里最主要的那个，这正是把「份额」的逻辑从事物挪到了原因。

abstract.en: Picture a plate where rice fills most of the surface and two small side dishes take the corners.
abstract.cn: 想象一只盘子，米饭占去大半个盘面，两样小菜只占边角。

abstract.en: A word for the largest share keeps the minority visible: mostly means not entirely, so the rest is still there.
abstract.cn: 一个表示最大份额的词始终让少数派可见：mostly 意为「并非全部」，剩下的部分仍在。

abstract.en: Because it measures shares rather than absolutes, mostly fits sentences that report, estimate and predict, from weather to polls.
abstract.cn: 因为它衡量的是份额而不是绝对，mostly 特别适合报告、估计和预测的句子，从天气到民调都是。

senses.title: Change of position
senses.definition: the process of changing position or place over time
senses.definitionCN: 随时间改变位置或处所的过程
senses.example: The motion of the pendulum is regular and easy to time.
senses.exampleCN: 钟摆的运动很规律，容易计时。
senses.why: Latin motio is simply a moving, from movere 'to move'; this is the plainest and oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 motio 就是「移动」，出自 movere「移动」；这是最直白、最古老的义项。

senses.title: A gesture that carries a message
senses.definition: a movement of the hand or head used instead of words to signal something
senses.definitionCN: 代替言语、用来示意的手部或头部动作
senses.example: With a quick motion of his hand, the conductor silenced the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 指挥手一挥，大厅便静了下来。
senses.why: A gesture is a small movement that does the work of a sentence.
senses.whyCN: 手势是一个小动作，却承担了一句话的功能。

senses.title: A proposal put to a meeting
senses.definition: a formal proposal presented at a meeting for discussion and a vote
senses.definitionCN: 在会议上正式提出、供讨论并表决的提议
senses.example: The motion to extend the deadline was carried by nine votes.
senses.exampleCN: 延长截止日期的动议以九票通过。
senses.why: To bring something forward is to move it onto the table; the proposal is the thing set in motion before the room.
senses.whyCN: 把某事提出来，就是把它移到桌面上；提议就是被推到全场面前的东西。

senses.title: A request made to a court
senses.titleCN: 向法庭提出的程序申请
senses.definition: a formal request asking a court to make a ruling or take an action
senses.definitionCN: 请求法庭作出裁定或采取行动正式申请
senses.example: The defence filed a motion to dismiss the charge.
senses.exampleCN: 辩方提交了撤销指控的动议。
senses.why: A court, like an assembly, decides only what is moved before it, so the legal request kept the parliamentary name.
senses.whyCN: 法庭和议会一样，只裁决被推到它面前的事，因此法律申请沿用了议会里的名称。

senses.title: The act of starting a process
senses.definition: the act of setting a plan, process or event going
senses.definitionCN: 使计划、进程或事件开始运转的动作
senses.example: One phone call set the whole rescue in motion.
senses.exampleCN: 一个电话启动了整场救援。
senses.why: The fixed phrase set in motion treats a process as a body that must be pushed before it will move.
senses.whyCN: 「使……启动」这一固定说法把进程当作一具必须先推一把才会动的身体。

senses.title: The running of a machine
senses.definition: the working movement of a machine or mechanism, or its state of running
senses.definitionCN: 机器或机构的运转动作，或其正在运行的状态
senses.example: The old lift was in motion again after the belt was replaced.
senses.exampleCN: 换过皮带后，老电梯又运转起来。
senses.why: A machine is a body whose parts move, so its operation is naturally called motion.
senses.whyCN: 机器是一具有部件在动的身体，因此它的运行自然被叫作 motion。

senses.title: The moving works inside a device
senses.definition: the assembly of moving parts inside a device, especially a clock or watch
senses.definitionCN: 装置内部由运动部件组成的机构，尤指钟表机芯
senses.example: A watchmaker cleaned the motion and oiled each pivot.
senses.exampleCN: 钟表匠清理了机芯，并给每个轴心上了油。
senses.why: Watchmakers named the works by the movement they produce, and the term became the trade word for the whole mechanism.
senses.whyCN: 钟表匠以它所产生的运动来命名这套机构，这个说法后来成了整个机芯的行业词。

senses.title: To signal with the hand
senses.definition: to make a movement of the hand or head as a sign or direction
senses.definitionCN: 用手部或头部的动作作为信号或指引
senses.example: The usher motioned us toward the side door.
senses.exampleCN: 引座员示意我们往侧门走。
senses.why: The noun became a verb: to give a motion with the hand is to motion someone.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词：用手给出一个动作，就是向某人示意。

intro.en: Motion comes through Old French from Latin motio, a moving, built on the past-participle stem mot- of movere 'to move'. The proposal sense grows from bringing something forward, not from physical travel.
intro.cn: motion 经古法语来自拉丁 motio「移动」，由 movere「移动、推动」的过去分词词干 mot- 构成。动议义由「把某事提出来、推到面前」引申，并非来自物理位移。

items.en: Movere meant to move, to push away, to set in motion; its past-participle stem mot- is the base of the noun.
items.cn: movere 意为移动、推开、使动起来；它的过去分词词干 mot- 是名词的底子。

items.en: Motio, motionis named a moving or a movement; it is a third-declension noun built on the same stem.
items.cn: motio、motionis 指一次移动或运动；这是由同一词干构成的第三变格法名词。

items.en: Old French motion carried the noun into English in the fourteenth century, first as movement and soon after as a proposal.
items.cn: 古法语 motion 在十四世纪把这个名词带入英语，先指移动，不久也指提议。

items.en: English motion is recorded from the fourteenth century in the plain sense of movement, and in legal use soon afterwards.
items.cn: 英语 motion 自十四世纪有「移动」的直白用法记录，随后不久进入法律语境。

items.en: The sense of a proposal grows from the idea of bringing something forward, a motion made in a room rather than in space.
items.cn: 「提议」义从「把某事提出来」这一想法长出，是在房间里而非空间中做出的动作。

items.en: The first dates of the parliamentary and legal senses are approximate; the noun is well attested from the medieval period.
items.cn: 议会义与法律义的最早记录年代为约数；这个名词在中世纪已有充分记录。

note.en: The first group shares the stem of moving; the second group separates motion from a gesture, a proposal and a trend.
note.cn: 第一组共享「移动」的词干；第二组把 motion 与手势、提议、趋势等相邻说法区分开。

entries.definition: The verb and a common noun for a single act of moving; motion is the more formal noun of the process.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，也作普通名词指一次移动；motion 是更正式、指整个过程的名词。

entries.definition: From mot- plus -ive: the reason that moves a person to act, not the act of moving.
entries.definitionCN: 由「移动」词干加表倾向的词尾构成：推动人去行动的理由，不是移动的动作。

entries.definition: Built on the same stem with an agent ending: the thing that produces movement, as an engine does.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词干加表施动者的词尾：产生运动的东西，如发动机。

entries.definition: Com- 'together' plus motion: a confused rushing about of people, a movement that is noisy.
entries.definitionCN: 表「一起」的拉丁前缀加「移动」：人群慌乱地涌动，一种喧闹的移动。

entries.definition: Not a form of motion and from a different source: it comes from a separate Latin noun for an instant or a weight, and in English it names a point in time rather than a movement.
entries.definitionCN: 不是 motion 的一种形式：它来自另一个拉丁名词，指瞬间或重量；英语中它指时间上的一点，而非移动。

entries.definition: Movement in general, often of a group or a trend; motion is more often a single act or a formal proposal.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指运动，常指一群人的行动或趋势；motion 更常指单次动作或正式动议。

entries.definition: A deliberate movement of the body that communicates; motion can be any movement, gesture is always meaningful.
entries.definitionCN: 有传达作用的身体动作；motion 可以是任何动作，gesture 一定带有意义。

entries.definition: A plan offered for consideration; a motion is a proposal put formally to a meeting.
entries.definitionCN: 提出供考虑的计划；motion 是正式提交会议表决的提议。

entries.definition: The ability to move from place to place, used of animals and vehicles rather than of processes.
entries.definitionCN: 从一处到另一处移动的能力，多用于动物与交通工具，而非抽象过程。

entries.definition: The speed at which something moves; motion names the fact of moving, not how fast.
entries.definitionCN: 移动的快慢；motion 说的是「在动」这件事，不涉及快慢。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin root, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁词根、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Movere is Latin for move, and mot- is its participle stem.
normal.cn: movere 是拉丁语「移动」，mot- 是它的分词词干。

normal.en: The family runs motion, motionless, motive, motor, commotion.
normal.cn: 同族词有 motion、motionless、motive、motor、commotion。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the everyday senses: in motion, slow motion, set in motion, motion picture.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出日常义：在运动中、慢动作、启动、电影。

normal.en: Law says a motion to dismiss is a formal request, not a physical move.
normal.cn: 法律上的「撤销动议」是正式申请，不是物理移动。

normal.en: Physics describes motion with velocity and acceleration, two ways of measuring how it changes.
normal.cn: 物理用速度与加速度描述运动，这是衡量它如何变化的两种方式。

abstract.en: Picture a chess piece sliding one square, leaving a pale trail behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚棋子滑过一格，身后留下一道浅痕。

abstract.en: Picture a hand lifted at a meeting, and the room falling silent before a word is spoken.
abstract.cn: 想象会议上一只手抬起，还没开口，全场就静了。

abstract.en: Picture a key turned in a lock and a whole machine waking up.
abstract.cn: 想象钥匙在锁里一转，整台机器醒了过来。

examples.en: The motion of the tide is charted twice a day.
examples.cn: 潮水的运动每天被记录两次。

examples.en: Her motion to reopen the case was rejected.
examples.cn: 她要求重审此案的动议被驳回了。

examples.en: The camera records motion in the dark by sensing heat.
examples.cn: 这台摄像机在黑暗中靠感热来记录运动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「mo（摸）+ tion（神）」——摸一下就走，身子一动；motion 运动、动议

root: 拉丁 movere「移动、推动」→ 过去分词词干 mot- → 拉丁 motio「移动」→ 古法语 motion → 英语 motion；会议动议义由「提出、推动」引申。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one push: a body changes place, a hand makes a sign, an idea is pushed before a meeting, a request before a court, a process is started, a machine runs, its works are named, and finally the hand itself becomes a verb.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个「推」展开：身体换位、手做出信号、想法被推到会议前、申请被推到法庭前、进程被启动、机器运转、机芯得名，最后手本身变成动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger pushes a piece from one square to the next, and the piece leaves a trail.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指把棋子从一格推到下一格，棋子拖出一道痕迹。

branches.en: THE PLAIN MOVE: a body changes place, and one small move of the hand carries a message.
branches.cn: 直白的动：身体换位，而手的一个小动作传达信息。

branches.en: BROUGHT BEFORE OTHERS: the same push places a proposal before a meeting or a request before a court.
branches.cn: 推到众人面前：同一个推力把提议放到会议前，或把申请放到法庭前。

branches.en: SET GOING: a process is pushed into motion, and a machine keeps moving once it starts.
branches.cn: 使之启动：进程被推入运动，机器一旦启动便持续运转。

branches.en: THE WORKS: the parts that carry the movement inside a watch take the name of movement itself.
branches.cn: 机芯：钟表内部承担运动的那套部件，直接以「运动」命名。

branches.en: THE VERB: the hand that made the sign becomes the act of motioning.
branches.cn: 动词：做出信号的那只手，变成「示意」这个动作。

intro.en: Motion is a Latin noun of moving, and the stem mot- builds verbs, agents and a whole English family.
intro.cn: motion 是表示「移动」的拉丁名词，词干 mot- 还构成动词、施动者名词与整个英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin movere gives motio and motion, and also motive, motor, commotion and momentum; the ending -tion names an action or its result.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 movere 衍生 motio 与 motion，也衍生 motive、motor、commotion 与 momentum；后缀 -tion 表示动作或结果。

items.example: The root supplies the push behind every sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根为每个义项提供「推」的底子。

items.example: The Latin noun names the act of moving.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词指移动这一动作。

items.example: She rose to put a motion to the committee.
items.exampleCN: 她起身向委员会提出动议。

items.example: The cat lay motionless under the chair.
items.exampleCN: 猫一动不动地躺在椅子下。

items.example: A commotion broke out at the gate.

items.meaning: a reason that moves a person

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词后缀
items.example: The ending turns a verb of moving into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「移动」的动词变成名词。

latinEntries.meaning: to move, push, set in motion

definition_zh: 发动机；马达；汽车；机动的；运动（神经）的
definition_en: a machine that turns energy into movement; a car, in British informal use; and, as an adjective, relating to engine-driven vehicles or to the body's own movement

scene: 修车间的木架上放着一台拆开的旧机器，铜线圈露在外面，地上掉着几颗螺丝。A rusty electric motor lay on the bench, its copper coil exposed.
sceneCN: 这里是「电动机、马达」（第 1 个义项：把能量转成转动的机器）；句意为木架上放着一台生锈的电动机，铜线圈露在外面。图中可辨识物件：木架、铜线圈、散落的螺丝。

由 motor 与 way 复合而成，义为「高速公路」
由 motor 加 -ize 构成，义为「使机动化；给……装上发动机」

senses.title: A machine that turns energy into movement
senses.definition: a machine that uses electricity or fuel to produce movement and drive another machine
senses.definitionCN: 用电或燃料产生运动、驱动另一台机器的装置
senses.example: The fan stopped when its motor burned out.
senses.exampleCN: 风扇的电动机烧坏后就不转了。
senses.why: Latin motor meant a mover, one that sets something else going, and English applied the name to the machine that does exactly that inside another machine.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 motor 意为「推动者」，即让别的东西动起来的那一方；英语把这个名字给了在另一台机器内部干这件事的装置。

senses.title: A car in British speech
senses.definition: a car, especially in informal British English
senses.definitionCN: 汽车，尤用于英式口语
senses.example: They packed the children into the motor and drove north.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把孩子们塞进车里，开车往北去。
senses.why: Once the engine was the interesting part of a vehicle, British speech began calling the whole vehicle a motor, keeping the machine's name for the thing it drove.
senses.whyCN: 当发动机成了一辆车里最要紧的部分，英式口语干脆把整辆车都叫 motor，用机器名代替它所驱动的东西。

senses.title: Belonging to engine-driven vehicles
senses.definition: connected with vehicles that have engines, or with the trade that makes and sells them
senses.definitionCN: 与装有发动机的车辆有关的，或与制造、销售这类车辆的行业有关的
senses.example: The motor trade hired fewer school leavers that year.
senses.exampleCN: 那一年汽车行业招收的毕业生减少了。
senses.why: The noun grew an adjective without changing shape: anything belonging to engine-driven vehicles could take the word as a label, so motor trade and motor vehicle need no suffix.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词没变形就长出了形容词用法：凡属于发动机驱动车辆的事物，直接拿这个词当标签就行，于是 motor trade、motor vehicle 都不必再加词尾。

senses.title: Belonging to the body's movement system
senses.definition: connected with the nerves and muscles that produce movement in the body
senses.definitionCN: 与身体中产生运动的神经和肌肉有关的
senses.example: The injury damaged the motor nerves in his left hand.
senses.exampleCN: 这次受伤损伤了他左手的运动神经。
senses.why: Physiologists needed a word for the body's own movers, the nerves and muscles that carry out a command, and motor was the obvious borrow from mechanics.
senses.whyCN: 生理学家需要给身体里执行指令的推动者——神经与肌肉——一个名字，于是从机械学里直接借来了 motor 这个词。

intro.en: Motor is the Latin agent noun for a mover, taken into English in the nineteenth century and then extended from engines to cars and to the body's nerves.
intro.cn: motor 是拉丁语里表示「推动者」的施动名词，十九世纪进入英语，随后从发动机扩展到汽车与身体的神经。

items.en: Movere meant to move or to set in motion, and it stands behind a large family of English words about movement.
items.cn: movere 意为移动、使动起来，英语里一大族与运动有关的词都出自它。

items.en: Motor was a Latin noun for the mover, the one who or that which sets something in motion, though it was much rarer than the verb beside it.
items.cn: motor 是拉丁语名词，指推动者，即让某物动起来的人或物；不过比起旁边的动词，它出现得要少得多。

items.en: English took motor with the rise of machines driven by steam and electricity, using it first for the source of motion and then for the engine itself.
items.cn: 随着蒸汽与电力驱动的机器兴起，英语借入了 motor，先指运动的来源，再指发动机本身。

items.en: By the early twentieth century British speakers were calling a car a motor, a shortening of motor car, and the word entered everyday speech.
items.cn: 到二十世纪初，英式说法开始把汽车叫作 motor，这是 motor car 的缩短形式，这个词由此进入日常口语。

items.en: Modern English keeps the engine noun, the British car noun, the vehicle adjective, and the physiological adjective for nerves and skills.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了这个名词指发动机、英式口语里指汽车、形容词指车辆，以及生理学上形容神经与技能。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin mover family; the near-meaning group collects words for engines and for the vehicles they drive.
note.cn: 形近组顺着拉丁语「移动」词族展开；近义组收表示发动机以及它所驱动车辆的词。

entries.definition: Movement, or a formal proposal put to a meeting.
entries.definitionCN: 运动；会议上正式提出的动议。

entries.definition: A reason that makes someone act.
entries.definitionCN: 促使人行动的理由。

entries.definition: To raise someone in rank or help something advance.
entries.definitionCN: 提升某人的职位，或推动某事进展。

entries.definition: A strong feeling that moves a person.
entries.definitionCN: 推动人的强烈情绪。

entries.definition: A machine that turns fuel into motion.
entries.definitionCN: 把燃料转成运动的机器。

entries.definition: A machine that produces electricity.
entries.definitionCN: 产生电力的机器。

entries.definition: A road vehicle with four wheels and its own engine.
entries.definitionCN: 自带发动机的四轮道路车辆。

entries.definition: A machine used for carrying people or goods.
entries.definitionCN: 用来运送人或货物的机器。

normalIntro.en: A Latin agent noun runs through the family, so every sense of the word names something that moves other things rather than something that is moved.
normalIntro.cn: 一个拉丁语施动名词贯穿这个词族，所以这个词的每个义项都在给「推动别的东西」的那一方命名，而不是被推动的一方。

normal.en: Movere is the Latin verb to move, and motor is its agent noun, the one that moves, which is why a motor is never the thing moved but the thing that moves others.
normal.cn: movere 是拉丁语「移动」，motor 是它的施动名词，指「推动者」；所以 motor 从来不是被推动的东西，而是推动别的东西的那一方。

normal.en: The -or ending in motor is the same agent ending found in actor and doctor, so the word literally names a doer.
normal.cn: motor 里的 -or 与 actor、doctor 里的施动词尾相同，所以这个词字面上就是在给一个「做事的角色」命名。

normal.en: Motorist adds -ist to motor, a person who uses a motor vehicle, which shows how a machine name turned into a name for its driver.
normal.cn: motorist 在 motor 后加 -ist，指使用机动车的人，可见机器名如何变成了驾驶者的名字。

normal.en: Motorway is motor plus way, a road built for motor traffic, a compound that says exactly what the road is for.
normal.cn: motorway 是 motor 加 way，指为机动车修的路；这个复合词把路的用途说得明明白白。

normal.en: The physiological sense keeps the original meaning best: motor nerves are the body's own movers, the ones that carry out a command.
normal.cn: 生理学义最贴近原意：运动神经就是身体自己的推动者，负责把指令执行下去。

abstract.en: Picture a coil spinning inside an iron shell, turning current into a steady push.
abstract.cn: 想象一圈线圈在铁壳里旋转，把电流变成一股持续的推力。

abstract.en: A word that names the mover rather than the movement shows how English labels a machine by its role, not by its shape.
abstract.cn: 一个为「推动者」而不是「运动」命名的词，说明英语常按角色给机器命名，而不是按外形。

abstract.en: The same noun reaches from a factory engine to the nerves in a hand, because both are places where a command becomes motion.
abstract.cn: 同一个名词从工厂里的发动机一直伸到手上的神经，因为这两处都是「指令变成运动」的地方。

examples.en: The fan stopped when its motor burned out.
examples.cn: 风扇的电动机烧坏后就不转了。

examples.en: They packed the children into the motor and drove north.
examples.cn: 他们把孩子们塞进车里，开车往北去。

examples.en: The injury damaged the motor nerves in his left hand.
examples.cn: 这次受伤损伤了他左手的运动神经。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摩托」——摩托车里的摩托就是 motor 的音译，本指推动的那台机器；记住 motor 是发动机，也指汽车。

root: 拉丁语 movere（移动）的施动名词 motor（推动者）进入英语，十九世纪起指发动机，二十世纪英式口语又指汽车；同族词有 motion、motive、promote、emotion。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the thing that sets something else moving; the senses divide into the engine, the British car, the vehicle adjective, and the body's own movers.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「让别的东西动起来的那一方」；义项分出机器、英式口语的汽车、车辆的形容词用法，以及身体自己的推动者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a copper coil spinning inside an iron shell and turning current into a steady push.
core.cn: 核心意象：一圈铜线在铁壳里旋转，把电流变成持续的推力。

branches.en: a coil spinning inside a rusted casing
branches.cn: 生锈外壳里旋转的一圈线圈

branches.en: a fan blade turning in a hot room
branches.cn: 热房间里转动的风扇叶

branches.en: children bundled into a small car on a cold morning
branches.cn: 冷天早晨被塞进一辆小车的孩子

branches.en: a factory gate where new cars roll out
branches.cn: 新车驶出的工厂大门

branches.en: a hand opening slowly after a nerve signal arrives
branches.cn: 接到神经信号后慢慢张开的手

intro.en: A Latin agent noun, the verb behind it, and a few English suffixes carry motor from a mover to engines, cars and nerves.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁语施动名词、它背后的动词，以及几个英语词尾，把 motor 从「推动者」带到发动机、汽车与神经。

latinIntro.en: Latin movere and its agent noun motor supply the whole family, while motus and motivus show the movement and the force that causes it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的 movere 及其施动名词 motor 支撑起整个词族，motus 与 motivus 则分别表示运动与引起运动的力量。

senses.title: A multi-lane road for fast motor traffic

senses.why: Once the roads had a name of their own, the name came to stand for the whole network and the shared experience of driving on it.

intro.en: Motorway is a straightforward English compound of motor and way, coined in the early twentieth century when Britain began building roads reserved for motor vehicles.
intro.cn: motorway 是 motor 与 way 构成的直白英语复合词，二十世纪初英国开始修建机动车专用道路时被造出来。

items.en: Movere meant to move, and motor, its agent noun, named the thing that sets others moving.
items.cn: movere 意为移动，其施动名词 motor 指让别的东西动起来的那一方。

items.en: Via was the Latin word for a road or way, the notion English later expressed with its Germanic word way.
items.cn: via 是拉丁语里「道路」一词，英语后来用日耳曼语源的 way 表达同一概念。

items.en: English had long made compounds like railway and carriageway, so motorway followed a familiar pattern once motor traffic existed.
items.cn: 英语早有 railway、carriageway 这类复合词，一旦机动车出现，motorway 便顺着这个熟悉的模式被造出来。

items.en: Britain opened its first purpose-built motorway in 1958, and the word settled into everyday use with the new roads.
items.cn: 英国于 1958 年开通第一条专用高速公路，这个词随新路一道进入日常用语。

items.en: Modern English keeps motorway as the standard British term; American English prefers freeway or expressway for the same kind of road.
items.cn: 现代英语中 motorway 是标准英式说法；美式英语对同类道路更常用 freeway 或 expressway。

note.en: The look-alike group collects compounds built on motor or way; the near-meaning group gathers the other words English uses for high-speed roads.
note.cn: 形近组收以 motor 或 way 构成的复合词；近义组收英语里表示高速道路的其他说法。

entries.definitionCN: 美式英语对快速城市或城际道路的另一种称呼。

entries.definition: A general word for a main public road; broader than motorway, which names the special fast class.

normalIntro.en: The word says what it is: a way reserved for motors, and the family around it follows the same plain pattern.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把自身说清楚了：一条留给 motor（机动车）的路，它周围的词族也遵循同样直白的构词方式。

normal.en: Motorway is motor plus way, literally a road for motor vehicles, with nothing hidden in the compound.
normal.cn: motorway 是 motor 加 way，字面就是「机动车走的路」，复合词里没有任何隐藏含义。

normal.en: Compare railway: the same word way is used, only the vehicle changes, rail for trains and motor for cars.
normal.cn: 对比 railway：用的是同一个 way，只是交通工具换了——rail 给火车，motor 给汽车。

normal.en: Motorist and motorway share the same base, so the driver and the road both belong to the motor family.
normal.cn: motorist 与 motorway 共用同一个基础词，驾车者和这条路都归在 motor 词族之下。

normal.en: Freeway, expressway and motorway all end in way, which is English's favorite ending for a named class of road.
normal.cn: freeway、expressway、motorway 都以 way 结尾，这是英语给各类道路命名时最爱的词尾。

normal.en: British usage reserves motorway for the special grade-separated roads, so the word is narrower than highway.
normal.cn: 英式用法里 motorway 专指立体交叉的特殊道路，因此它比 highway 的范围窄。

sceneCN: 这里 movement 指有共同诉求的群体性运动（第 3 个义项：社会运动）；句意：这场运动从几名学生开始，很快站满了广场。图中可辨识物件：手写标语牌、扩音器、横幅、统一的袖标；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 运动；移动；动作；社会运动；乐章；走势

derivatives.zh: 移动；搬动；感动
可移动的；不固定的
可移动性
推动者；搬运者
移动的；感人的

senses.title: Change of position
senses.definition: the act or process of changing position or place
senses.definitionCN: 改变位置或处所的动作或过程
senses.example: A slow movement of the shelf warned that the wall was settling.
senses.exampleCN: 架子缓缓移位，说明墙体在下沉。
senses.why: Movement is the native noun of the verb move, and its oldest sense is simply the fact of changing place.
senses.whyCN: movement 是动词 move 的本族名词，最古老的意思就是「换了地方」这件事。

senses.title: A single action of the body
senses.definition: one deliberate action or gesture, especially of the hand or body
senses.definitionCN: 一次有意的动作或姿态，尤指手或身体的
senses.example: With one movement she folded the letter and sealed it.
senses.exampleCN: 她一个动作就把信折好封上了。
senses.why: A process can be cut into single acts, and one of those acts is also called a movement.
senses.whyCN: 一个过程可以切成一个个单独的动作，其中一次也叫 movement。

senses.title: An organized campaign for a cause
senses.titleCN: 为某一诉求组织起来的社会运动
senses.definition: a group of people acting together over time to bring about a change in society or policy
senses.definitionCN: 一群人长期共同行动，以求改变社会或政策
senses.example: The movement for clean rivers spread from one town to the whole valley.
senses.exampleCN: 洁净河流的运动从一个镇扩展到整个河谷。
senses.why: In the nineteenth century people acting together were seen as one body on the move, so a campaign became a movement.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪，人们把共同行动的一群人看作一个在移动的整体，于是运动便成了一项社会运动。

senses.title: A section of a musical work
senses.titleCN: 长篇乐曲中的一个乐章
senses.definition: a self-contained part of a long musical composition, such as a symphony
senses.definitionCN: 长篇乐曲（如交响曲）中相对独立的一部分
senses.example: The second movement is slow and almost silent.
senses.exampleCN: 第二乐章缓慢而近乎无声。
senses.why: Music was thought of as advancing in stages; each stage is a movement within the whole work.
senses.whyCN: 人们把音乐想成一段段向前推进；每一个阶段就是整部作品里的一个乐章。

senses.title: A trend in figures or opinion
senses.definition: a change in level, price or opinion over time, seen as a direction
senses.definitionCN: 水平、价格或舆论随时间的变化，被看作一个方向
senses.example: The upward movement in rents began before the new bridge opened.
senses.exampleCN: 租金的上涨走势在新桥通车前就开始了。
senses.why: A line on a chart that keeps going one way looks like something travelling, so a trend is called a movement.
senses.whyCN: 图表上一直朝一个方向走的线，看起来像有东西在行进，因此趋势也被称为 movement。

senses.title: The mechanism inside a clock
senses.definition: the assembly of moving parts that drives a clock or watch
senses.definitionCN: 驱动钟表的整套运动部件
senses.example: The watch has a hand-wound movement and a glass back.
senses.exampleCN: 这块表是手上链机芯，背面是玻璃的。
senses.why: Watchmakers named the works by the movement they produce, and the term became the trade word for the whole mechanism.
senses.whyCN: 钟表匠以它产生的运动来命名这套机构，这个说法后来成了整个机芯的行业词。

senses.title: A relocation of troops or supplies
senses.definition: the organized moving of troops, ships or supplies from one place to another
senses.definitionCN: 有组织地把部队、船只或物资从一处移到另一处
senses.example: Satellite images tracked the movement of trucks along the border.
senses.exampleCN: 卫星图像追踪了卡车沿边境的调动。
senses.why: A body of men or goods changing place is still the plain sense, made formal by military use.
senses.whyCN: 一批人或货物换地方，仍是那个直白的意思，只是被军事用法正式化了。

senses.title: A bowel movement
senses.definition: an act of emptying the bowels, used as a neutral medical term
senses.definitionCN: 排空肠道的一次动作，用作中性的医学说法
senses.example: The nurse recorded the patient's movements after surgery.
senses.exampleCN: 护士记录了病人术后的排便情况。
senses.why: Medicine needed a plain, polite noun for a bodily action, and the ordinary word for moving served.
senses.whyCN: 医学需要一个平实而礼貌的词来指这一身体动作，于是用了「移动」这个普通词。

intro.en: Movement comes through Old French movement from movoir, the French form of Latin movere 'to move'. The musical and social senses are later growths from the plain idea of something advancing.
intro.cn: movement 经古法语 movement 来自 movoir，即拉丁 movere「移动」的法语形式。乐章义与社会运动义都是后来的引申，源自「某物在向前推进」这一朴素想法。

items.en: Movere meant to move, to set going, and it is the source of the whole French and English family.
items.cn: movere 意为移动、使动，是整个法语与英语词族的源头。

items.en: The French verb movoir or moveir meant to move and gave English the verb move.
items.cn: 法语动词 movoir 或 moveir 意为移动，并给英语带来了动词 move。

items.en: The noun movement named the act of moving; it uses the same action-noun ending as many French words in -ment.
items.cn: 名词 movement 指移动这一动作；它用的动作名词词尾，与许多以 -ment 结尾的法语词相同。

items.en: English took the noun in the fourteenth century, at first for physical movement and later for a single action.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪引入这个名词，起初指物理移动，后来也指单次动作。

items.en: From the eighteenth century a movement named a section of a symphony or sonata, following the idea of music advancing by stages.
items.cn: 从十八世纪起，movement 指交响曲或奏鸣曲中的一个部分，沿用「音乐分段推进」的想法。

items.en: The collective sense for a campaign is a nineteenth-century growth, when large groups acting for a cause were described as one moving body.
items.cn: 指社会运动的集体义是十九世纪长出的，当时为某一诉求行动的大群人是被当作一个移动的整体来描述。

note.en: The first group shares the verb move and is often mistaken for the noun; the second group separates movement from motion, campaign and trend.
note.cn: 第一组共享动词 move，常与这个名词混淆；第二组把 movement 与 motion、campaign、trend 等词区分开。

entries.definition: The verb and a countable noun for one act of moving; movement is the noun of the process or the campaign.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，也可数名词指一次移动；movement 指过程或社会运动。

entries.definition: Move plus -able: able to be moved, said of furniture or a feast day; it is an adjective, not an act.
entries.definitionCN: 由动词加表「能够」的词尾构成：可被移动的，用于家具或不固定的节期；是形容词，不是动作。

entries.definition: Move plus -ing: either in the act of moving or able to stir the feelings, as a moving speech does.
entries.definitionCN: 由动词加表进行或性质的词尾构成：或指正在移动，或指能打动人心，如感人的演讲。

entries.definition: A shortened form of moving picture, from the moving images on film; it is a thing, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 「活动影像」一词的缩略，来自胶片上移动的影像；指作品，不是动作。

entries.definition: Move plus -er: a person or thing that moves something, or a company that transports goods.
entries.definitionCN: 由动词加表施动者的词尾构成：推动某事的人或物，也指搬家公司。

entries.definition: Often a single physical act or a formal proposal; movement is wider and covers campaigns and trends.
entries.definitionCN: 多指单次物理动作或正式动议；movement 范围更宽，还涵盖社会运动与趋势。

entries.definition: An organized series of actions for a goal; a movement is broader and longer, and usually social.
entries.definitionCN: 为某目标组织的一系列行动；movement 更宽、更久，通常带社会性。

entries.definition: A strong effort or campaign to reach a target, often official; it stresses the push, not the people.
entries.definitionCN: 为达目标的有力推动或活动，常是官方发起的；强调推动力，不强调人群。

entries.definition: The general direction in which something is changing; movement can name a change in figures but is more concrete.
entries.definitionCN: 事物变化的总方向；movement 也能指数字变动，但更具体。

entries.definition: The ability to move from place to place, used of animals and vehicles; it is technical and not social.
entries.definitionCN: 从一处到另一处移动的能力，用于动物和交通工具；属技术用语，不含社会义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin root, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁词根、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Movere is Latin for move, and movement is the noun made from the French verb.
normal.cn: movere 是拉丁语「移动」，movement 是由法语动词变来的名词。

normal.en: The family runs move, movable, moving, movie, mover.
normal.cn: 同族词有 move、movable、moving、movie、mover。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: social movement, slow movement, upward movement.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：社会运动、慢乐章、上升走势。

normal.en: The -ment ending turns an action into a noun, as in agreement and management.
normal.cn: 名词词尾把动作变成名词，如「同意」与「管理」二词。

normal.en: A clock's movement is the works that keep it moving, a trade term from watchmaking.
normal.cn: 钟表的 movement 是让它持续运转的机芯，这是制表业的行业说法。

abstract.en: Picture one person walking, then a hundred walking in the same direction.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人走，然后一百个人朝同一个方向走。

abstract.en: Picture a symphony advancing one stage at a time, each stage its own room.
abstract.cn: 想象一部交响曲一段段向前走，每个阶段自成一间屋子。

abstract.en: Picture a line on a graph climbing and someone calling that climb a movement.
abstract.cn: 想象图表上一条线往上爬，有人把这段爬升叫 movement。

examples.en: The movement of goods across the border slowed after the flood.
examples.cn: 洪水过后，货物过境的流动变慢了。

examples.en: The civil rights movement changed the town's hiring rules.
examples.cn: 民权运动改变了这座小镇的用工规定。

examples.en: A thermostat senses the movement of air through the duct.
examples.cn: 恒温器感知空气在管道中的流动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「move（挪）+ ment（门特）」——挪一挪，人群就成了一场运动；movement 移动、运动、乐章

root: 拉丁 movere「移动」→ 古法语 movoir「移动」→ 古法语名词 movement「移动、动作」→ 英语 movement；乐章义由乐曲内部的推进，社会运动义为十九世纪集体行动的用法。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one body in motion: it changes place, makes a single act, gathers into a campaign, advances as a section of music, climbs as a trend, drives a clock, moves as troops, and passes as a bodily function.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个「在动的身体」展开：它换位、做出一次动作、聚成一场运动、作为乐曲的一部分推进、作为趋势上升、驱动机芯、作为部队调动，最后成为一种身体功能。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of people walking together in one direction, their steps forming an advancing line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一队人朝同一方向走，脚步连成一条推进的横线。

chain: A LINE ON A CHART RISES

branches.en: PLAIN MOVING: one body changes place, and one deliberate action of the hand is carved out of it.
branches.cn: 直白的动：一具身体换了地方，其中切出手的一次有意动作。

branches.en: PEOPLE TOGETHER: many bodies moving for one cause become a social movement.
branches.cn: 众人同行：许多身体为一个诉求而动，聚成社会运动。

branches.en: A WORK IN STAGES: music advancing by sections gives the musical movement its name.
branches.cn: 分段推进的作品：音乐按段落向前，乐章由此得名。

branches.en: A CLIMB ON A CHART: the same advance is read as a trend in figures.
branches.cn: 图表上的爬升：同一种推进被读成数字的走势。

branches.en: MOVING PARTS AND BODIES: a watch's works, a column of trucks, and the bowels all carry the plain sense into new settings.
branches.cn: 运动部件与身体：钟表机芯、车队与肠道，都把直白义带进新的场合。

intro.en: Movement is a French action noun built on the Latin verb of moving, with the same ending that forms many English nouns.
intro.cn: movement 是一个由拉丁「移动」动词构成的法语动作名词，用的词尾也构成许多英语名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin movere gives move, motion, motive and motor; the French noun movement adds the action-noun ending to the same verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 movere 衍生 move、motion、motive 与 motor；法语名词 movement 则在同一个动词上加动作名词词尾。

items.example: The verb supplies the push behind every sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词为每个义项提供「推」的底子。

items.example: The French verb passed into English as move.
items.exampleCN: 这个法语动词进入英语后成为 move。

items.meaning: the act of moving; a campaign
items.example: The movement began with a few students.
items.exampleCN: 这场运动从几名学生开始。

items.example: The machine's movements are smooth and silent.
items.exampleCN: 这台机器的各个动作平顺而安静。

items.meaning: to shift; to touch the feelings
items.example: Move the chair closer to the window.
The stage has a movable floor.
items.exampleCN: 这个舞台有一块可移动的地板。

items.example: It was a moving account of the flood.
items.exampleCN: 那是对洪水的感人叙述。

items.example: The movie ran for two hours.
items.exampleCN: 这部电影放映了两个小时。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词后缀
items.example: It is the same ending as in management and agreement.
items.exampleCN: 它与 management 和 agreement 用的是同一个词尾。

latinEntries.meaning: to move, push, set in motion

definition_zh: 电影；影片；电影院；看电影这项活动；电影业
definition_en: a film shown in a cinema or on a screen, also the cinema as a place or an outing and the film industry as a whole
core_image: 暗下来的放映厅里，一束光穿过空气打在幕布上
scene: 老街上的影院门口排起长队，售票窗口的灯还亮着。They queued outside the old cinema for a late-night movie.
sceneCN: 这里是「电影、影片」（第 1 个义项：放映的故事片）；句意为他们为一场深夜电影在旧影院外排队。图中可辨识物件：影院门口、排队的人群、售票窗。

pos.zh: 电影；影片；电影院；看电影这项活动；电影业

derivatives.zh: 由 movie 与 goer 复合而成，义为「经常看电影的人」
由 movie 与 maker 复合而成，义为「电影制片人；导演」
由 movie 与 going 复合而成，义为「看电影这件事；常看电影的」

senses.title: A film shown on a screen
senses.definition: a story or record told in moving images and sound, shown in a cinema or on a screen
senses.definitionCN: 用活动影像和声音讲述的故事或记录，在影院或屏幕上放映
senses.example: We watched a movie about a fishing village.
senses.exampleCN: 我们看了一部关于渔村的电影。
senses.why: The word is a clipped form of moving picture, so the moving image itself is the starting point of every sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是「活动的画面」的缩写，所以每一个义项都从「画面在动」这一点开始。

senses.title: The cinema as a place or an outing
senses.titleCN: 电影院；看电影这项活动
senses.definition: the cinema, or an occasion of going there to watch a film
senses.definitionCN: 电影院，或去那里看电影的一次活动
senses.example: They spent the afternoon at the movies.
senses.exampleCN: 他们一下午都泡在电影院里。
senses.why: Because a movie is what is shown, the plural the movies came to name the place and the outing built around it.
senses.whyCN: 因为被放映的东西是 movie，复数 the movies 就转而指放映它的场所，以及围绕它安排的一次出门。

senses.title: The film industry
senses.definition: the business of making and distributing films, especially in a particular country
senses.definitionCN: 制作与发行影片的行业，尤指某一国家的电影业
senses.example: He has worked in the movies for thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 他在电影业干了三十年。
senses.why: A product made by many hands naturally names the whole trade that produces it, so the plural also stands for an industry.
senses.whyCN: 由许多人之手做出来的产品，自然会用来指生产它的整个行业，于是复数也代表一个产业。

senses.title: A short video made for any screen
senses.definition: a short filmed piece made for a phone, a website or a home screen rather than a cinema
senses.definitionCN: 为手机、网站或家庭屏幕而非影院制作的短小影片
senses.example: She made a short movie on her phone.
senses.exampleCN: 她用手机拍了一段短片。
senses.why: Once the word means moving images rather than a cinema release, any screen can host a movie, and length stops being essential.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词指的是活动影像而不是影院上映，任何屏幕都能放映 movie，长度也就不再是必要条件。

intro.en: Movie is not an ancient word: it was cut down from moving picture in the early days of cinema and then spread from the screen to the place and the trade.
intro.cn: movie 并不是古词：它由早期的「活动的画面」缩短而来，随后从屏幕扩展到场所与行业。

items.en: The verb movere meant to move or set in motion, and it lies behind the English move inside moving picture.
items.cn: 动词 movere 意为移动、使动，它藏在 moving picture 里的英语 move 背后。

items.en: Old French movoir carried the Latin verb into English use and gave English the plain verb move.
items.cn: 古法语 movoir 把这个拉丁动词带入英语，给英语留下了朴素的动词 move。

items.en: The phrase moving picture was coined when photographs first appeared to move, and it described a new kind of show.
items.cn: 当照片第一次看上去会动时，人们造出 moving picture 这一说法，用来描述一种新的表演。

items.en: American speakers shortened moving picture to movie with the familiar -ie ending also seen in talkie, a film with sound.
items.cn: 美国使用者把 moving picture 缩短为 movie，用了熟悉的 -ie 词尾，带声音的影片 talkie 也用了这个词尾。

items.en: Modern English extends movie from the film itself to the cinema, the outing and the industry, and now to short videos on any screen.
items.cn: 现代英语把 movie 从影片本身扩展到电影院、看电影的出门活动与电影业，如今还指任何屏幕上的短片。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms on the move stem inside moving picture, while the near-meaning group collects other words for films and their showing.
note.cn: 形近组收「活动的画面」里那条表示移动的词干上的形式，近义组收其他指影片及放映的词。

entries.definition: To change position, the verb hidden inside moving picture.
entries.definitionCN: 改变位置；藏在 moving picture 里的动词。

entries.definition: An act of moving, or an organized group working for a cause.
entries.definitionCN: 移动的动作，或为某个目标组织起来的群体。

entries.definition: Changing position, or causing a strong feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 正在移动的，或引起强烈情感的。

entries.definition: A person who goes to the cinema, often regularly.
entries.definitionCN: 常去电影院看电影的人。

entries.definition: A motion picture, the word more common in British usage.
entries.definitionCN: 电影，英式用法中更常见的词。

entries.definition: A building where films are shown, or the art of making them.
entries.definitionCN: 放映影片的建筑，或制作影片的艺术。

entries.definition: A film, especially in older or informal British use.
entries.definitionCN: 影片，尤见于较早或非正式的英式用法。

entries.definition: Recorded film material, especially before it is edited.
entries.definitionCN: 拍摄下来的影像素材，尤指尚未剪辑的部分。

normalIntro.en: The word is a clipped compound, and its family keeps returning to the idea of images that move.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一个被截短的复合词，它的同族词也一直回到「画面会动」这个念头。

normal.en: Movie is moving picture cut short, with the -ie ending that also turned talking picture into talkie.
normal.cn: movie 是 moving picture 缩短而来，用的 -ie 词尾也曾把 talking picture 变成 talkie。

normal.en: The plural the movies names the place and the habit, not a pile of separate films.
normal.cn: 复数的 the movies 指场所与习惯，而不是一堆各自分开的影片。

normal.en: movie theater and movie star are compounds: one names the building, the other the person the screen makes famous.
normal.cn: movie theater 与 movie star 都是复合词：一个指建筑，一个指屏幕捧红的人。

normal.en: A moviegoer is simply movie plus goer, the person who goes.
normal.cn: moviegoer 就是 movie 加 goer，指去看电影的人。

normal.en: Latin movere, to move, sits far back inside the word, which is why the family is full of movement words.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 movere（移动）藏在这个词的很深处，所以这一族词里全是表示「动」的词。

abstract.en: Twenty-four pictures a second make a still photograph stand up and walk.
abstract.cn: 每秒二十四张画面，能让一张静止的照片站起来走路。

abstract.en: A dark hall, one beam of light, and a whole town living inside it for two hours.
abstract.cn: 一间暗厅，一束光，一整个小镇在里面过上两个小时。

abstract.en: The word began as a description of a trick and ended as the name of an industry.
abstract.cn: 这个词起初只是对一种戏法的描述，最后成了一个行业的名字。

examples.en: The movie was shot in a small mountain town.
examples.cn: 这部电影在一个山间小镇拍摄。

examples.en: We go to the movies most Fridays.
examples.cn: 我们大多数周五都去看电影。

examples.en: She wants to work in the movies after college.
examples.cn: 她想大学毕业后进入电影业。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「木威」——一块木幕上放出很有威势的画面；记住 movie 是电影。

root: 一般认为 movie 是 moving picture（活动的画面）的缩写；moving 源自古法语 movoir、拉丁语 movere（移动），-ie 是英语指小词尾。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the film itself; the senses then divide into the place and the outing, the industry behind it, and the short video on any screen.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是影片本身；义项由此分出放映的场所与出门活动、背后的产业，以及任何屏幕上的短片。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a beam of light cutting through a dark hall and landing on a screen.
core.cn: 核心意象：一束光穿过黑暗的放映厅，落在幕布上。

branches.en: a beam of light crossing a dark hall
branches.cn: 一束光穿过黑暗的放映厅

branches.en: a queue forming outside a cinema
branches.cn: 影院外排起的队伍

branches.en: credits rolling over a crowded studio lot
branches.cn: 片尾字幕滚过拥挤的片场

branches.en: a short clip filmed on a phone
branches.cn: 用手机拍下的一段短片

branches.en: a late show that turns into a night out
branches.cn: 一场深夜电影变成一次夜游

intro.en: The word is a clipped compound resting on a Latin verb of motion, an English ending, and compounds that name the people and the buildings around films.
intro.cn: 这个词是被截短的复合词，依托一个表示运动的拉丁动词、一个英语词尾，以及为人和建筑命名的复合形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin movere and its noun motus name movement, and they are the distant source of the move inside moving picture.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 movere 及其名词 motus 表示移动，是 moving picture 里 move 的遥远来源。

definition_zh: 许多；大量；非常；…得多；差不多
definition_en: a large amount of something, to a great degree, and in fixed phrases nearly or hardly
core_image: 一只不断被添满的碗，米粒堆过了碗沿
scene: 工地上堆着还没搬完的砖，屋顶的瓦片只铺了一半。There is much work left before the roof is finished.
sceneCN: 这里是「许多、大量」（第 1 个义项：大量的事物）；句意为屋顶完工前还有大量活要干。图中可辨识物件：砖堆、半铺的屋顶、瓦片。

derivatives.zh: 由 much 加 -ness 构成，义为「大量；许多」，多见于固定说法 much of a muchness，意为彼此差不多
由 much 加 -ly 构成，非正式用语，义为「非常；大大地」
由前缀 over-（过度）加 much 构成，义为「过多的；过多地」

senses.title: A large amount of something
senses.definition: a large amount or quantity of something, especially with uncountable nouns
senses.definitionCN: 某事物的大量或许多，尤与不可数名词连用
senses.example: Much of the old town was rebuilt after the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水过后，老城的很大一部分被重建了。
senses.why: The Old English word meant great in size, and size easily becomes amount when the thing counted cannot be divided.
senses.whyCN: 古英语这个词本指体积大，而当所计的东西分不开时，体积就很容易变成数量。

senses.title: To a great degree
senses.definition: by a large amount, especially before comparatives or verbs of liking
senses.definitionCN: 大量地，尤用于比较级或表示喜好的动词之前
senses.example: I much prefer walking to driving in this weather.
senses.exampleCN: 这种天气里，我远更喜欢走路而不是开车。
senses.why: Once great size is abstracted, it can measure intensity rather than quantity, so the word starts to mean very or far.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「体积大」被抽象化，它就能衡量强度而非数量，于是这个词开始表示「很」或「远远」。

senses.title: Nearly, in fixed phrases
senses.definition: almost, used in phrases such as much the same or much as
senses.definitionCN: 几乎，用于 much the same 或 much as 一类短语
senses.example: The two maps are much the same.
senses.exampleCN: 这两张地图几乎一模一样。
senses.why: Two things that are much the same have come so close that the remaining difference is tiny, so greatness of degree turns into nearness.
senses.whyCN: 两样东西「大致相同」，说明它们靠得如此近，剩下的差别很小，于是程度之大转成了「接近」。

senses.title: Not a good example of a type, in negative phrases
senses.definition: used in not much of a to say that someone or something is a poor example of a type
senses.definitionCN: 用于 not much of a，表示某人或某物算不上某一类型的好例子
senses.example: He is not much of a cook, but he tries.
senses.exampleCN: 他算不上好厨师，但他肯尝试。
senses.why: If much measures amount, then not much of a thing measures a small amount of that quality, which is a polite way of saying it is poor.
senses.whyCN: 如果 much 衡量的是数量，那么 not much of a thing 就是衡量那种品质的数量很少，这是说它水准不高的委婉方式。

intro.en: Much descends from an Old English adjective for great, and its irregular more and most come from the same root rather than from -er and -est.
intro.cn: much 源自一个表示「大的」的古英语形容词，它的不规则比较级 more 与最高级 most 同出这一词根，而不是靠 -er 与 -est。

items.en: A reconstructed root generally written meg- meant great, and it also produced Latin magnus and Greek megas.
items.cn: 一般认为，一个常写作 meg- 的印欧语重构词根意为「大的」，它也产生了拉丁语 magnus 与希腊语 megas。

items.en: Old English mycel meant great or much, and its comparative and superlative were ma and mæst.
items.cn: 古英语 mycel 意为大的、多的，它的比较级与最高级是 ma 与 mæst。

items.en: Middle English shortened muchel to muche, and the clipped form much became standard.
items.cn: 中古英语把 muchel 缩短为 muche，截短后的 much 成为标准形式。

items.en: By the early modern period much was fixed for amount and degree, while more and most kept the old comparative and superlative.
items.cn: 到近代早期，much 已固定用来表示数量与程度，而 more 与 most 保留了古老的比较级与最高级。

items.en: Modern English much works as determiner, pronoun and adverb, and appears mainly in questions, negatives and fixed phrases.
items.cn: 现代英语的 much 可作限定词、代词和副词，主要出现在疑问句、否定句和固定短语中。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the irregular family built on the same old root, while the near-meaning group collects other quantity and degree words.
note.cn: 形近组收同一古老词根上的不规则词族，近义组收其他表示数量与程度的词。

entries.definition: The comparative of much, meaning a greater amount.
entries.definitionCN: much 的比较级，表示更大的量。

entries.definition: The superlative of much, meaning the greatest amount.
entries.definitionCN: much 的最高级，表示最大的量。

entries.definition: The quality of being much, used in much of a muchness.
entries.definitionCN: 「多」的性质，见于 much of a muchness。

entries.definition: More than is needed or wanted.
entries.definitionCN: 超过所需或所愿的。

entries.definition: A large number of countable things, the counterpart of much.
entries.definitionCN: 大量可数的事物，与 much 相对。

entries.definition: Enough or more than enough of something.
entries.definitionCN: 足够或绰绰有余的量。

entries.definition: To a very large degree.
entries.definitionCN: 在很大程度上；非常。

entries.definition: A large amount, in everyday speech.
entries.definitionCN: 日常口语中的大量。

normalIntro.en: The word is an old Germanic adjective of size that turned into a measure of amount and then of degree.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼语中表示体积的古老形容词，先变成数量的度量，再变成程度的度量。

normal.en: Old English mycel meant great, and its shortened descendant much kept the idea of a large mass.
normal.cn: 古英语 mycel 意为大的，缩短后的后代 much 保留了「一大团」的意思。

normal.en: More and most are not formed with -er and -est because they are relics of the old comparative and superlative.
normal.cn: more 与 most 不是用 -er 和 -est 构成的，因为它们是古老比较级与最高级的遗存。

normal.en: Much pairs with uncountable nouns such as water and time, while many pairs with things you can count.
normal.cn: much 与 water、time 这类不可数名词搭配，many 则与可以数的东西搭配。

normal.en: too much, very much and how much are fixed patterns that cover excess, intensity and quantity.
normal.cn: too much、very much 与 how much 是固定说法，分别覆盖过量、强度与数量。

normal.en: not much of a cook means a poor cook, because the phrase measures how little of the quality is present.
normal.cn: not much of a cook 意为算不上好厨师，因为这个说法衡量的是那种品质有多少。

abstract.en: A bowl that is filled past its rim is the picture behind every use of much.
abstract.cn: 一只堆过碗沿的碗，就是 much 每次使用背后的画面。

abstract.en: Size becomes amount, amount becomes intensity, and intensity becomes nearness: one root, three directions.
abstract.cn: 体积变成数量，数量变成强度，强度变成接近：一条根，三个方向。

abstract.en: English keeps the old irregular more and most as a reminder that this word is older than its grammar.
abstract.cn: 英语保留不规则的 more 与 most，提醒人这个词比它的语法规则更老。

examples.en: Much of the old town was rebuilt after the flood.
examples.cn: 洪水过后，老城的很大一部分被重建了。

examples.en: I much prefer walking to driving in this weather.
examples.cn: 这种天气里，我远更喜欢走路而不是开车。

examples.en: The two maps are much the same.
examples.cn: 这两张地图几乎一模一样。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马吃」——马吃东西吃得多，就是许多；记住 much 是许多。

root: 古英语 mycel（大的、多的）经中古英语 muchel 缩短为 much；比较级 more、最高级 most 同出这一词根，一般认为与拉丁语 magnus 同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a large amount; the senses then divide into a high degree, a nearness in fixed phrases, and the negative phrase that measures a poor example.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是大量；义项由此分出很高的程度、固定短语里的「接近」，以及衡量「算不上好」的否定说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bowl filled again and again until the grain piles over its rim.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只被反复添满的碗，米粒堆过了碗沿。

branches.en: a bowl filled past its rim
branches.cn: 一只堆过碗沿的碗

branches.en: a road chosen over a faster one
branches.cn: 放着更快的路不走，偏选这一条

branches.en: two maps laid side by side
branches.cn: 两张并排摊开的地图

branches.en: a kitchen trial that ends in smoke
branches.cn: 一次以浓烟收场的厨房尝试

branches.en: a store of grain that dwarfs the need
branches.cn: 一堆远超所需的粮食

intro.en: The word is an old adjective of size with an irregular comparative family, plus two English suffixes that build a noun and an adverb from it.
intro.cn: 这个词是表示体积的古老形容词，带着一个不规则比较级词族，另有两个英语后缀从它造出名词与副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin magnus, magis and maximus belong to the same old root as much, even though English took the word through Germanic channels.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 magnus、magis 与 maximus 和 much 同出一个古老词根，尽管英语是经由日耳曼语渠道得到这个词的。

definition_zh: 泥；烂泥；泥浆；泥料；淤泥；污名
definition_en: wet soft earth, the same material used for building, fine sediment in water and, figuratively, dirt thrown at a reputation
core_image: 雨后路上被车轮碾出的两道深沟，泥水顺着沟沿往外渗
scene: 雨下了一夜，村口的土路被车轮碾出两道深沟。The truck's wheels sank deep into the mud.
sceneCN: 这里是「泥、烂泥」（第 1 个义项：湿软的泥土）；句意为卡车的轮子深陷泥中。图中可辨识物件：土路、车辙、车轮。

pos.zh: 泥；烂泥；泥浆；泥料；淤泥；污名

collocations.zh: 泥饼（儿童用泥做的假饼）

derivatives.zh: 由 mud 加 -y 构成，义为「泥泞的」；作动词指「使浑浊」
由 mud 与 guard 复合而成，义为「挡泥板」
由 mud 与 flat 复合而成，义为「潮间带的泥滩」
由 mud 与 slinging 复合而成，义为「竞选中的抹黑攻击」

senses.title: Wet, soft earth
senses.definition: soft wet earth that sticks to shoes and wheels
senses.definitionCN: 湿软、会粘在鞋和车轮上的泥土
senses.example: The truck's wheels sank deep into the mud.
senses.exampleCN: 卡车的轮子深陷泥中。
senses.why: The Germanic word names the soft, sticky ground itself, so the physical sensation of sticking is the centre of the meaning.
senses.whyCN: 这个日耳曼词指的就是那种软而黏的地面本身，所以「黏住」的身体感觉是词义的中心。

senses.title: Earth and water used as building material
senses.definition: clay or earth mixed with water and shaped or spread while wet
senses.definitionCN: 黏土或泥土加水调成，趁湿塑形或涂抹的材料
senses.example: The old walls were built of mud and straw.
senses.exampleCN: 那些老墙是用泥和草茎砌成的。
senses.why: If mud is soft ground, it can also be handled and shaped, so the same word names the raw material of a wall.
senses.whyCN: 既然泥是软的地面，它也能被捧起来塑形，于是同一个词又指砌墙的原料。

senses.title: Fine sediment at the bottom of water
senses.definition: fine particles that settle on the bed of a river, lake or sea
senses.definitionCN: 沉在河、湖或海底的细小颗粒
senses.example: The river bed was covered with thick black mud.
senses.exampleCN: 河床上覆盖着厚厚的黑泥。
senses.why: Mud carried by water eventually settles, and the settled layer keeps the name of the wet earth that made it.
senses.whyCN: 被水带走的泥终究会沉下来，沉积的那一层仍沿用形成它的湿土之名。

senses.title: A reputation dirtied in public
senses.definition: used in phrases such as drag someone's name through the mud to mean public accusation and disgrace
senses.definitionCN: 用于「drag someone's name through the mud」一类说法，指公开指责与名誉受损
senses.example: The scandal dragged his name through the mud.
senses.exampleCN: 那桩丑闻把他的名声拖进泥里。
senses.why: Being covered in mud is visible and humiliating, so the image transfers neatly to a reputation covered in public accusation.
senses.whyCN: 浑身沾泥既显眼又难堪，于是这个画面很自然地转到被公开指责覆盖的名声上。

intro.en: Mud is a Germanic word for soft wet earth, probably reaching English from Low German, and it has no reliable Latin relative.
intro.cn: mud 是日耳曼语中表示湿软泥土的词，可能经低地德语进入英语，它没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

items.en: A reconstructed stem often written mud- is generally thought to underlie the Germanic words for wet earth, though its exact shape is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为，一个常写作 mud- 的日耳曼语重构词干是各语言表示湿土的词的底子，但其确切形式并不确定。

items.en: Low German mudde is the form most often cited as the immediate source of the English word.
items.cn: 低地德语 mudde 是最常被引为英语这个词直接来源的形式。

items.en: Middle English mudde appeared in the thirteenth century for soft wet ground and for the mire of streets.
items.cn: 中古英语 mudde 在十三世纪出现，指湿软的地面，也指街道上的泥泞。

items.en: The spelling settled as mud, and the word spread to building material and to river sediment.
items.cn: 拼写定型为 mud，词义也扩展到建筑材料与河底沉积物。

items.en: Modern English mud keeps the literal ground sense and supplies the image behind phrases about ruined reputations.
items.cn: 现代英语的 mud 保留字面的泥土义，并为关于名誉受损的短语提供画面。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built on the mud stem, while the near-meaning group collects other words for soft wet ground and sediment.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在 mud 词干上的形式，近义组收其他表示湿软地面与沉积物的词。

entries.definition: Covered with mud, or to make something unclear.
entries.definitionCN: 沾满泥的，或使某物变得浑浊。

entries.definition: A cover that keeps mud off a wheel.
entries.definitionCN: 挡住车轮泥水的护板。

entries.definition: Low muddy ground left bare by the tide.
entries.definitionCN: 退潮后露出的低洼泥地。

entries.definition: The practice of attacking a rival's reputation in public.
entries.definitionCN: 公开攻击对手名声的做法。

entries.definition: A thin, slippery, unpleasant wet substance.
entries.definitionCN: 稀薄、湿滑而令人不适的物质。

entries.definition: Fine earth carried by water and left as sediment.
entries.definitionCN: 被水带来并沉积下来的细土。

entries.definition: Heavy, sticky earth that can be shaped when wet.
entries.definitionCN: 湿时可塑形的厚重黏土。

entries.definition: Thick, soft, dirty material, often industrial waste.
entries.definitionCN: 浓稠、柔软而肮脏的物质，常指工业废泥。

normalIntro.en: The word names the soft ground itself, and its family keeps adding things to it or moving it with water.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词指的就是那种软的地面本身，同族词则不断给它加东西，或让它随水流动。

normal.en: Mud probably came into English from Low German mudde, which is why its shape is so short and plain.
normal.cn: mud 很可能从低地德语 mudde 进入英语，所以它的词形才如此短而朴素。

normal.en: muddy adds -y to mud: full of mud, therefore unclear and stained.
normal.cn: muddy 在 mud 后加 -y，意为「满是泥的」，因此也指浑浊与沾污。

normal.en: mudguard and mudflat are compounds: one stops mud, the other names ground the tide leaves bare.
normal.cn: mudguard 与 mudflat 都是复合词：一个挡住泥，一个指潮水退后露出的泥地。

normal.en: Mud is uncountable, so one says a lot of mud rather than many muds.
normal.cn: mud 不可数，所以说 a lot of mud，而不说 many muds。

normal.en: The phrase drag a name through the mud turns the visible stain of earth into a public stain on honour.
normal.cn: 「drag a name through the mud」这个说法把泥土可见的污迹变成名誉上公开的污点。

abstract.en: Mud is what water does to solid ground when it stays too long.
abstract.cn: 泥是水在实地上停留太久之后做出来的东西。

abstract.en: Every footprint is mud remembering the shape of a shoe for a little while.
abstract.cn: 每个脚印都是泥暂时记住一只鞋的形状。

abstract.en: The same stuff that builds a wall can also dirty a name.
abstract.cn: 砌得起墙的东西，也能弄脏一个名字。

examples.en: The truck's wheels sank deep into the mud.
examples.cn: 卡车的轮子深陷泥中。

examples.en: Rain turned the path into a river of mud.
examples.cn: 雨水把小路变成了一条泥河。

examples.en: The children built castles out of mud.
examples.cn: 孩子们用泥堆起了城堡。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马的」——马的在泥里踩出一串深坑；记住 mud 是泥。

root: 中古英语 mudde 可能来自低地德语 mudde，指湿软的泥土；一般认为与日耳曼语表示湿土的词干有关，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is wet soft earth; the senses then divide into building material, river sediment, and the figurative stain on a reputation.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是湿软的泥土；义项由此分出建筑材料、河底沉积物，以及名誉上的比喻性污迹。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two deep wheel ruts in a village road after a night of rain.
core.cn: 核心意象：下了一夜雨，村口土路上被车轮碾出的两道深辙。

branches.en: boots pulling free of a wet path
branches.cn: 靴子从湿路上拔出来

branches.en: hands shaping a wall from wet earth
branches.cn: 用手把湿土糊成墙

branches.en: a river bed layered with dark silt
branches.cn: 河床积着黑色的淤泥

branches.en: a headline that soils a reputation
branches.cn: 一条把名声弄脏的标题

branches.en: mud on a shoe and mud on a name

definition_zh: 木乃伊；干尸；（英式儿语）妈妈
definition_en: a dead body preserved by embalming or by natural drying, especially one from ancient Egypt
core_image: 一具被布条层层缠住的遗体，皮肤干成皮革，眼睛的位置只剩两个深窝
scene: 展柜里的遗体被布条层层缠住，皮肤干成深褐色，标签写着出土地点。The mummy lay in the case, wrapped in layer upon layer of linen, its skin dried to a dark brown.
sceneCN: 这里 mummy 指「经防腐或自然干燥而保存下来的遗体」（第 1 个义项：人工或自然形成的干尸）；句意为展柜里一具木乃伊被层层亚麻布包裹，皮肤干成深褐色。可辨识物件：亚麻布、展柜、干枯的手。

senses.title: An embalmed body
senses.definition: a dead body preserved by embalming so that it does not decay
senses.definitionCN: 经防腐处理、因而不腐坏的遗体
senses.example: The mummy was wrapped in linen and laid in a painted case.
senses.exampleCN: 这具木乃伊用亚麻布包裹，安放在彩绘棺匣里。
senses.why: The word first named a medicinal substance from embalmed bodies, then the bodies themselves.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指从防腐尸体中取得的一种药，随后才指尸体本身。

senses.title: An Egyptian mummy
senses.definition: a body preserved by the Egyptian embalming tradition
senses.definitionCN: 按埃及防腐传统保存下来的遗体
senses.example: The Egyptian mummy was scanned without opening its wrappings.
senses.exampleCN: 这具埃及木乃伊未拆裹布就做了扫描。
senses.why: Egyptian examples were so famous that the word became almost a proper label for them.
senses.whyCN: 埃及的实例过于著名，这个词几乎成了它们的专称。

senses.title: A naturally dried body
senses.definition: a body dried by sand, wind or cold before decay could proceed
senses.definitionCN: 在腐坏开始前被沙、风或寒冷干燥保存的遗体
senses.example: The desert mummy was preserved by dry air rather than by resin.
senses.exampleCN: 这具沙漠干尸靠干燥空气而非树脂保存下来。
senses.why: Once the body, not the method, defines the word, natural drying also counts.
senses.whyCN: 一旦定义这个词的是遗体而非处理方法，自然干燥也算在内。

senses.title: An animal mummy
senses.definition: a preserved animal body, often a sacred or companion animal
senses.definitionCN: 被保存下来的动物遗体，常为圣兽或陪伴动物
senses.example: Cat mummies were sold as offerings in the temple courts.
senses.exampleCN: 猫木乃伊在神庙庭院里作为供品出售。
senses.why: The practice extended to animals, and the word followed without a separate term.
senses.whyCN: 这种做法扩展到动物，词也随之延伸，并未另造新词。

senses.title: Mother, in British nursery speech
senses.definition: a child's word for mother, from a different nursery syllable
senses.definitionCN: 儿童对母亲的称呼，来自另一个儿语词
senses.example: The child ran to her mummy at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子跑向门口的妈妈。
senses.why: This homonym comes from the nursery word mum, not from Arabic mumiya, and the two histories never touch.
senses.whyCN: 这个同形词来自儿语词 mum，而非阿拉伯语 mumiya，两条来历从未交汇。

senses.title: The bitumen drug of the old name
senses.definition: the medicinal substance formerly prepared from embalmed bodies or from bitumen
senses.definitionCN: 旧时取自防腐尸体或沥青的药用物质
senses.example: Apothecaries sold mummy as a cure for bruises.
senses.exampleCN: 旧时药剂师把木乃伊药当作治跌打的药出售。
senses.why: Arabic mumiya named bitumen, and the drug sense came before the body sense in English.
senses.whyCN: 阿拉伯语 mumiya 指沥青，英语中「药」义先于「遗体」义出现。

senses.title: A dried-out, gaunt person
senses.definition: a living person who looks dried out and stiff
senses.definitionCN: 看起来干枯僵硬的活人
senses.example: He came back from the desert a mummy of his former self.
senses.exampleCN: 他从沙漠回来，成了昔日自己的干尸。
senses.why: The metaphor uses the mummy's dryness and stiffness, not its death.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻取的是木乃伊的干与僵，而非它的死亡。

senses.title: Mummy brown pigment
senses.definition: a brown pigment formerly made from ground mummy remains
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用研磨的木乃伊遗骸制成的棕色颜料
senses.example: Mummy brown was used for shadows until supplies ran out.
senses.exampleCN: 木乃伊棕曾被用来画阴影，直到原料耗尽。
senses.why: The pigment trade named the colour after its source, and the colour outlived the practice.
senses.whyCN: 颜料贸易以原料给颜色命名，而颜色比这种做法活得更久。

intro.en: Mummy began as the name of bitumen and a medicine, then shifted to the embalmed bodies that supplied it; English also has a separate nursery word mummy for mother. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: mummy 先是沥青与一种药的名称，后转到提供这种药的防腐尸体上；英语另有一个指母亲的儿语同形词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Persian mum meant 'wax', and the word passed into Arabic as the name of a bituminous substance.
items.cn: 波斯语 mum 意为「蜡」，这个词进入阿拉伯语后指一种沥青状物质。

items.en: Arabic mumiya named bitumen, especially the pitch used in embalming, and also the preserved body that contained it.
items.cn: 阿拉伯语 mumiya 指沥青，尤指防腐所用的沥青，也指含有沥青的保存遗体。

items.en: Medieval Latin mumia and Old French momie carried the word to Europe as a drug made from ground mummy.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁 mumia 与古法语 momie 把这个词带到欧洲，指用研磨木乃伊制成的药。

items.en: By the seventeenth century English mummy meant the embalmed body itself, and Egypt became its most famous source.
items.cn: 到 17 世纪，英语 mummy 已指防腐遗体本身，埃及则成为最著名的来源地。

items.en: The nursery word mummy for mother comes from mum, a reduplicated infant sound, and is unrelated to the Arabic word.
items.cn: 指母亲的儿语 mummy 来自 mum，即婴儿重复的音节，与阿拉伯语词无关。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): why mummified flesh was called a wax word is not established, and the earliest English use of the body sense has no exact citation, so any earlier date offered is provisional.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：为何把防腐遗体用「蜡」词称呼，尚无定论；英语中遗体义的最早使用没有确切书证，凡给出的更早年代都是暂定的。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like mummy but belong to other roots; group two holds other ways of naming a preserved body.
note.cn: 第一组是与 mummy 形近却另有词源的词；第二组是其他指保存遗体的说法。

entries.definition: The short nursery word for mother; mummy is its diminutive, unrelated to the Arabic burial word.
entries.definitionCN: 指母亲的儿语短词；mummy 是它的指小形式，与阿拉伯语埋葬词无关。

entries.definition: From Middle English momelen 'to speak indistinctly', probably imitative of closed lips.
entries.definitionCN: 来自中古英语 momelen「含糊地说」，大概模仿闭唇的声音。

entries.definition: From Old French momerie 'masking, buffoonery', with a different origin and meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 来自古法语 momerie「戴面具、滑稽表演」，来源与含义都不同。

entries.definition: From Russian mamont, a name for a large extinct elephant; it looks like mummy but shares nothing.
entries.definitionCN: 来自俄语 mamont，指已灭绝的大型象；看似与 mummy 相近，实则毫无关联。

entries.definition: The neutral word for a dead body, with no suggestion of preservation.
entries.definitionCN: 指遗体的中性词，不含保存之意。

entries.definition: A formal or medical word for a dead body, from Latin cadere 'to fall'.
entries.definitionCN: 正式或医学用语，来自拉丁 cadere「倒下」。

entries.definition: A body preserved by injecting or coating with preservatives, whether or not wrapped.
entries.definitionCN: 经注射或涂覆防腐剂保存的遗体，不论是否裹布。

entries.definition: The remains or belongings of a holy person, kept for veneration.
entries.definitionCN: 受尊崇者的遗骸或遗物，供人敬奉。

normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：阿拉伯语的沥青词、亚麻裹布，以及毫无关联的「妈妈」词。

normal.en: Arabic mumiya 'bitumen' is the source of the burial word.
normal.cn: 阿拉伯语 mumiya「沥青」是埋葬义的来源。

normal.en: The drug sense came before the body sense in English.
normal.cn: 英语中药义先于遗体义出现。

normal.en: Mummy for mother comes from mum, a nursery sound, and is unrelated.
normal.cn: 指母亲的 mummy 来自儿语 mum，与前者无关。

normal.en: Real compounds: mummy case, mummy cloth, mummy brown.
normal.cn: 真实复合词：木乃伊棺匣、木乃伊裹布、木乃伊棕。

normal.en: The plural is mummies, never mummys.
normal.cn: 复数作 mummies，不写作 mummys。

abstract.cn: 想象一具被裹得极紧的遗体，人变成了一个包裹。

abstract.en: Picture a face dried to leather, with the eyes reduced to two hollows.
abstract.cn: 想象一张干成皮革的脸，眼睛只剩两个深窝。

abstract.en: Picture a jar of dark medicine ground from something nobody now wishes to name.
abstract.cn: 想象一罐深色药粉，研磨自如今没人愿意点名的东西。

examples.en: The museum scanned the mummy without removing the wrappings.
examples.cn: 博物馆未拆裹布就对木乃伊做了扫描。

examples.en: Animal mummies were kept in jars as temple offerings.
examples.cn: 动物木乃伊被装在罐中作为神庙供品。

examples.en: The paint was mixed with mummy brown, a pigment no longer made.
examples.cn: 这颜料掺了木乃伊棕，一种如今不再生产的颜料。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「mummy」听似「妈咪」——裹得紧紧、像被妈妈抱住的干尸 → 木乃伊

root: 阿拉伯语 mumiya「沥青」（源自波斯语 mum「蜡」），经中世纪拉丁 mumia、古法语 momie 入英语；先指药，后指防腐遗体。指母亲的 mummy 来自儿语 mum，同形异源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from the embalmed body and its Egyptian and natural varieties, add animal mummies, then the unrelated mother word, the old bitumen drug, the gaunt-person metaphor and the pigment trade.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从防腐遗体出发，涵盖埃及与自然形成的类型，加入动物木乃伊，再转向无关的「妈妈」词、旧的沥青药、干瘪者的比喻与颜料贸易。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body wrapped into a package, dried until the face becomes leather and hollows.
core.cn: 核心意象：一具被裹成包裹的遗体，干到脸成皮革、只剩眼窝。

branches.en: EMBALMED BODY: the drug word settles on the bodies that supplied it, above all Egyptian ones.
branches.cn: 防腐遗体：「药」词落到提供药的遗体上，尤以埃及者为代表。

branches.en: DRYING WITHOUT RESIN: natural drying and animal burials widen the word beyond embalming.
branches.cn: 不用树脂的干燥：自然干尸与动物墓葬把词扩展到防腐之外。

branches.en: MOTHER HOMONYM: the nursery word shares spelling only.
branches.cn: 「妈妈」同形词：儿语词只共享拼写。

branches.en: MATERIAL TRADE: bitumen as medicine and ground remains as pigment both name a substance.
branches.cn: 材料贸易：沥青作药、遗骸研磨作颜料，命名的都是物质。

branches.en: DRY PERSON: the metaphor keeps dryness and stiffness, not death.
branches.cn: 干枯的人：比喻取干燥与僵硬，而非死亡。

intro.en: Mummy is a borrowed Arabic word, and its English family is built with Latin and Greek suffixes for making and processing.
intro.cn: mummy 是借入的阿拉伯语词，其英语词族用拉丁与希腊后缀构成「使成为」「处理过程」等义。

latinIntro.en: Arabic mumiya 'bitumen' gives mummy and mummify; the Latin suffix -ficare 'to make' and -atio 'process' build the rest.
latinIntro.cn: 阿拉伯语 mumiya「沥青」产生 mummy 与 mummify；拉丁后缀 -ficare「使成为」与 -atio「过程」构成其余部分。

items.meaning: wax; the source syllable of the Arabic word
items.example: Persian mum supplied the first syllable.
items.exampleCN: 波斯语 mum 提供了第一个音节。

items.example: Mumiya named the substance before the body.
items.exampleCN: mumiya 先指物质，后指遗体。

items.structure: Arabic mumiya through Medieval Latin and French
items.example: The mummy lay in a painted case.
items.exampleCN: 木乃伊躺在彩绘棺匣里。

items.meaning: to preserve a body as a mummy
items.example: They mummified the body with resin and linen.
items.exampleCN: 他们用树脂与亚麻布把遗体制成木乃伊。

items.meaning: the process of making a mummy
items.exampleCN: 木乃伊制作约需七十天。

items.example: The mummified hand was still wrapped.

items.meaning: the box that holds a mummy
items.example: The mummy case was painted blue.

items.meaning: the linen wrappings of a mummy
items.example: Mummy cloth was sold by the yard.
items.exampleCN: 木乃伊裹布曾按码出售。

items.meaning: a brown pigment made from mummy remains

latinEntries.structure: mumia, mumiae (f., first declension; Medieval Latin)
latinEntries.meaning: a medicinal preparation from embalmed bodies

definition_zh: 谋杀；凶杀；谋杀罪；糟蹋；彻底击败
definition_en: the crime of killing a person deliberately; to kill someone unlawfully and on purpose; also, in loose use, to ruin a piece of work or defeat an opponent completely
core_image: 一只手的影子按在另一个人的影子上，把对方从地面上抹去
scene: 侦探在雨后的巷口拉起警戒线，墙角的脚印还湿着，围观的人低声说这不像意外。The detective read the report and concluded that the man had been murdered in his own kitchen.
sceneCN: 这里是「谋杀、蓄意杀害」（第 1 个义项：非法且故意地夺去他人性命）；句意为侦探看过报告后断定这名男子是在自家厨房里被杀害的。图中可辨识物件：警戒线、湿脚印、厨房门。

pos.zh: 蓄意杀害；糟蹋；彻底击败

derivatives.zh: 由 murder 加表示「人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「凶手；谋杀者」
由 murder 加 -ous 构成，义为「蓄意杀人的；极其危险的」
由 murderer 加阴性后缀 -ess 构成，义为「女凶手」

senses.title: The crime of killing a person on purpose
senses.definition: the crime of killing another person deliberately and unlawfully
senses.definitionCN: 非法且故意地杀害他人的罪行
senses.example: The trial lasted two weeks and ended in a verdict of murder.
senses.exampleCN: 审判持续了两周，最终裁定为谋杀。
senses.why: Old English morthor named a hidden killing, a death kept secret, so the word first recorded concealment rather than the weapon.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 morthor 指暗中进行的杀害，是「不让外人知道的死亡」，所以这个词最早记录的重点是隐秘，而不是凶器。

senses.title: To kill a person unlawfully and deliberately
senses.definition: to kill someone on purpose and against the law
senses.definitionCN: 故意且违法地夺去他人生命
senses.example: Police believe the same person murdered two shopkeepers.
senses.exampleCN: 警方认为同一个人杀害了两名店主。
senses.why: Once the noun named the hidden act, the verb could name doing it, and the law uses the pair to separate a planned killing from an accident.
senses.whyCN: 名词既然指这种隐秘的行为，动词就能指做出这种行为；法律用这一对词把有预谋的杀害与意外区分开。

senses.title: Murder as a charge in law
senses.definition: the offence itself as charged in court, carrying the heaviest penalty in many legal systems
senses.definitionCN: 在法庭上被指控的罪名本身，在许多法律体系里对应最重的刑罚
senses.example: He was charged with murder and held without bail.
senses.exampleCN: 他被控谋杀，不得保释。
senses.why: Legal language turned the act into a countable charge, so murder can stand in a courtroom list beside theft and fraud.
senses.whyCN: 法律语言把这种行为变成一个可列举的罪名，于是 murder 能和盗窃、欺诈一起出现在法庭的罪名清单里。

senses.title: To ruin a performance or defeat an opponent badly
senses.definition: in informal use, to spoil a piece of work or beat an opponent by a wide margin
senses.definitionCN: 在口语中把作品弄坏，或以很大差距击败对手
senses.example: The young pianist murdered the difficult passage but never lost the audience.
senses.exampleCN: 那位年轻钢琴手把那一段难弹的乐句糟蹋了，却始终没有失去听众。
senses.why: The violent core image survives in slang as exaggeration: a singer who murders a song figuratively kills it, and the same hyperbole covers a heavy defeat.
senses.whyCN: 暴力的核心意象在俚语里以夸张的方式保留下来：歌手 murder 一首歌，就是把歌「弄死」了；同样的夸张也用来形容惨败。

intro.en: Murder is one of the oldest English words for killing, and its earliest use stresses secrecy rather than the manner of death.
intro.cn: murder 是英语里最古老的表示杀害的词之一，最早的用法强调的是隐秘，而不是死亡的方式。

items.en: Morthor named a secret killing, a death that the killer tried to hide, and the word kept that shadow of concealment.
items.cn: morthor 指私下进行的杀害，是凶手想要掩盖的死亡，这个词一直保留着隐瞒的阴影。

items.en: The verb morthrian meant to commit such a killing, and noun and verb travelled together into later English.
items.cn: 动词 morthrian 意为实施这类杀害，名词和动词一起进入了后来的英语。

items.en: Middle English murdren and murdre referred to both the act and the crime, and the modern spelling settled after the noun.
items.cn: 中古英语写作 murdren 与 murdre，兼指行为和罪名，现代拼写大致在名词之后固定下来。

items.en: Norman French gave English the legal pairing for a killing done with malice, and the courts kept murder apart from manslaughter.
items.cn: 诺曼法语给英语带来了「恶意杀害」的法律搭配，法庭把 murder 与过失杀人清楚分开。

items.en: Modern English keeps the criminal sense and adds a loose everyday sense in which a bad performance or a heavy defeat is called murder.
items.cn: 现代英语保留犯罪义，又加上日常的宽松用法，把糟糕的表演或惨败也称作 murder。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the family of murder plus two words that merely share its shape; the near-meaning group collects other verbs and legal terms for killing.
note.cn: 形近组收 murder 的同族词，以及两个只是字形接近的词；近义组收其他表示杀害的动词与法律术语。

entries.definition: The person who commits a murder.
entries.definitionCN: 实施谋杀的人。

entries.definition: Capable of or intending to kill; extremely dangerous.
entries.definitionCN: 有杀人意图的；极其危险的。

entries.definition: To speak quietly under the breath; only the shape resembles murder, the origins differ.
entries.definitionCN: 低声咕哝；只是字形接近 murder，词源不同。

entries.definition: A soft, low sound; the spelling is close but the word has a different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 轻柔低沉的声音；拼写相近，但词源不同。

entries.definition: To cause someone or something to die.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人或某物死亡。

entries.definition: To kill a prominent person, usually for political reasons.
entries.definitionCN: 通常出于政治原因刺杀要人。

entries.definition: To kill, especially violently, used mostly in old or literary texts.
entries.definitionCN: 杀害，尤指暴力杀害，多用于古旧或文学作品。

entries.definition: The killing of one person by another, whether lawful or not.
entries.definitionCN: 一人致另一人死亡，无论是否合法。

normalIntro.en: One old English noun of secret killing, its verb and its legal afterlife explain both the crime and the slang.
normalIntro.cn: 一个表示暗中杀害的古英语名词、它的动词，以及它在法律里的延续，同时解释了罪名与俚语。

normal.en: Old English morthor meant a secret killing, so the word begins with concealment rather than with blood.
normal.cn: 古英语 morthor 意为暗中的杀害，所以这个词起点是「隐瞒」，而不是血。

normal.en: Murderer adds -er, the person, while murderous adds -ous, the quality; both stay inside the criminal family.
normal.cn: murderer 加 -er 指人，murderous 加 -ous 指性质，两者都留在犯罪这个词族里。

normal.en: The law keeps murder, deliberate, apart from manslaughter, without intent, and the pair still defines the charge.
normal.cn: 法律把表示故意的 murder 与表示无意的 manslaughter 分开，这一对词至今界定着罪名。

normal.en: Noun and verb share one idea, so you can commit a murder or murder a person with no change of meaning.
normal.cn: 名词与动词共用一个意思，所以 commit a murder 与 murder a person 含义不变。

normal.en: The slang sense survives because murder is extreme, and exaggeration borrows extreme words for bad singing and heavy defeat.
normal.cn: 俚语义能留下来，是因为 murder 足够极端；夸张正好借极端词来形容走调的演唱和惨败。

abstract.en: Picture a shadow pressing another shadow into the ground until it disappears.
abstract.cn: 想象一个影子把另一个影子按进地面，直到它消失。

abstract.en: A word for a hidden death reminds you that concealment, not noise, was the original danger.
abstract.cn: 一个表示暗中死亡的词提醒人：最早的危险是掩盖，而不是声响。

abstract.en: Because it names an irreversible act, murder can be borrowed only loosely for a spoiled song or a lost match.
abstract.cn: 因为它指的是一种不可逆的行为，所以只能宽松地借来说糟蹋一首歌或输掉一场比赛。

examples.en: The court found that she had murdered her business partner.
examples.cn: 法庭认定她谋杀了她的生意伙伴。

examples.en: He was charged with murder after the body was found.
examples.cn: 尸体被发现后，他被控谋杀。

examples.en: Our team murdered them in the second half.
examples.cn: 我们队在下半场把他们彻底击败了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「抹的」——把人从世上抹掉，就是 murder；记住它是谋杀。

root: 古英语 morthor（暗中的杀害）与动词 morthrian 构成，中古英语作 murdre，诺曼法语强化了法律用法；同族词有 murderer、murderous，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a killing kept secret; the senses divide into the crime, the act, the legal charge, and a slang exaggeration.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是隐秘的杀害；义项分出罪行、行为、法律罪名，以及俚语里的夸张。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one shadow pressing another shadow flat against the ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个影子把另一个影子按平在地面上。

branches.en: a strip of tape sealing off a dark doorway
branches.cn: 封住黑暗门洞的警戒带

branches.en: a story told to neighbours that nobody believes
branches.cn: 讲给邻居听却没人相信的说法

branches.en: a hand doing what the law forbids
branches.cn: 做了法律禁止之事的那只手

branches.en: a charge read aloud in a courtroom
branches.cn: 法庭上被宣读的一项罪名

branches.en: a song shouted off key into a microphone
branches.cn: 对着麦克风走调喊完的一首歌

intro.en: An Old English noun and verb of secret killing, two English suffixes and the modern compounds carry the entry.
intro.cn: 一个表示暗中杀害的古英语名词与动词、两个英语后缀，以及现代复合形式，撑起了这个词条。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded: murder belongs to the Old English stock, and its relatives are Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录：murder 属于古英语词汇，其亲属词来自日耳曼语。

definition_zh: 肌肉；肌力；体力；影响力；实力
definition_en: body tissue made of fibres that can contract and produce movement, or the strength and power that such tissue gives
core_image: 一束束能自己收紧的绳索，一收紧就把相连的骨头拉动
scene: 健身房教练让学员把手贴上上臂，感受发力时那团组织的变化： He felt the muscle tighten under his hand.
sceneCN: 这里指「一块肌肉」（第 2 个义项：作为解剖单位的一块肌肉）；句意为他把手按在上臂，感到那块肌肉绷紧；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 力量；体力；（政治、军事上的）实力

forms.label: 形容词（肌肉的；肌肉发达的）
动词（强行挤入；使劲搬动）

derivatives.zh: 肌肉的；肌肉发达的；强有力的
肌肉系统；肌群
