senses.title: Contractile tissue
senses.titleCN: 肌肉组织：能收缩的纤维组织
senses.definition: tissue built from fibres that shorten when stimulated and so produce movement
senses.definitionCN: 由受刺激会缩短的纤维构成、从而产生运动的组织
senses.example: Skeletal muscle is built from long fibres that shorten when a nerve signal arrives.
senses.exampleCN: 骨骼肌由长纤维构成，神经信号到达时这些纤维会缩短。
senses.why: The core of the word is not shape but action: the tissue exists to pull, and only contraction makes it useful.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的核心不是形状而是动作：这种组织为拉动而生，只有收缩才使它有用。

senses.title: A single muscle organ
senses.titleCN: 一块肌肉：解剖学上的独立单位
senses.definition: one named bundle of muscle tissue with its own attachments, such as the biceps
senses.definitionCN: 一束有名称、有自身附着点的肌肉组织，如肱二头肌
senses.example: The surgeon repaired the muscle that controls the shoulder.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生修复了控制肩部的那块肌肉。
senses.why: Anatomy counts bundles rather than the material, so the mass of tissue becomes a countable organ with a name.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学按束计数而不按材料计数，于是整团组织变成有名字、可计数的器官。

senses.title: Smooth muscle
senses.titleCN: 平滑肌：内脏壁上的不随意肌
senses.definition: the involuntary muscle found in the walls of blood vessels and internal organs
senses.definitionCN: 分布于血管壁与内脏壁、不受意志控制的肌肉
senses.example: Smooth muscle in the artery wall narrows the vessel and raises blood pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 动脉壁的平滑肌使血管变窄，从而升高血压。
senses.why: The same contractile tissue works without orders from the will, so it is classified by where it sits and how it is controlled.
senses.whyCN: 同一种收缩组织可以不听意志指挥，因此按所在位置与控制方式另行分类。

senses.title: Cardiac muscle
senses.titleCN: 心肌：持续搏动的特化肌肉
senses.definition: the muscle of the heart wall, which contracts rhythmically without resting
senses.definitionCN: 心壁的肌肉，有节律地收缩且从不休息
senses.example: Cardiac muscle keeps beating without rest for a lifetime.
senses.exampleCN: 心肌一生都在跳动，从不休息。
senses.why: Heart muscle is a special case: it is striated like skeletal muscle but works continuously and involuntarily.
senses.whyCN: 心肌是个特例：它像骨骼肌一样有横纹，却持续工作且不受意志控制。

senses.title: Physical strength
senses.definition: the strength of the body, thought of as the power its muscles supply
senses.definitionCN: 身体的力量，被看作肌肉提供的力量
senses.example: It took real muscle to move the piano up the stairs.
senses.exampleCN: 把钢琴搬上楼确实费了不少力气。
senses.why: Strength is what muscle does, so the tissue name is used for the force itself, much as brains can stand for intelligence.
senses.whyCN: 力量是肌肉做的事，于是组织名称被用来指这种力，就像「头脑」一词可以指智力一样。

senses.title: Influence and pressure
senses.definition: power to make things happen, especially when used to push a plan through
senses.definitionCN: 推动事情办成的力量，尤指用来推动某项计划
senses.example: The mayor put muscle behind the housing plan and forced a vote.
senses.exampleCN: 市长为住房计划施加影响，推动了表决。
senses.why: Political force is imagined as bodily force: you lean on people the way a muscle leans on a load.
senses.whyCN: 政治力量被想象成身体力量：你对人施压，正如肌肉对重物施力。

senses.title: Military or economic power
senses.titleCN: 军事或经济实力（展示实力）
senses.definition: visible national or corporate power, displayed to discourage rivals
senses.definitionCN: 为震慑对手而展示的国家或企业实力
senses.example: The country showed its military muscle in a large joint exercise.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家通过大规模联合演习展示军事实力。
senses.why: The display is the point: the tissue is shown rather than used, and the show is meant to be seen and feared.
senses.whyCN: 展示本身就是目的：实力被亮出来而不一定真正使用，亮的目的是让人看见并忌惮。

senses.title: Muscle memory
senses.titleCN: 肌肉记忆：熟练到无需思考的动作
senses.definition: movement skills stored so deeply by practice that they feel automatic
senses.definitionCN: 经反复练习深植、几乎自动完成的动作技能
senses.example: After years of practice, the moves are stored in muscle memory.
senses.exampleCN: 多年练习之后，这些动作已存入肌肉记忆。
senses.why: The body seems to remember what the mind no longer rehearses, so the tissue is credited with the memory.
senses.whyCN: 身体似乎记住了头脑不再预演的东西，于是这份记忆被归到肌肉名下。

intro.en: Muscle goes back to Latin musculus, literally little mouse, a diminutive of mus mouse. The image is usually explained as a moving bulge under the skin. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: muscle 可追溯到拉丁语 musculus，字面义「小老鼠」，是 mus「老鼠」的指小形式。一般认为这个形象来自皮下随动作鼓动的一块。年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin musculus meant both a little mouse and a muscle. Roman writers already used it for the fleshy moving parts of the body.
items.cn: 拉丁 musculus 既指「小老鼠」，也指「肌肉」。罗马作家已用它指身体中会鼓动的肉。

items.en: The common explanation is that a muscle moving under the skin looked like a mouse running beneath cloth. This is generally accepted as an image, but it is a popular explanation rather than a documented ancient statement.
items.cn: 通常的解释是：皮下活动的肌肉像一只在布下跑动的老鼠。这一形象一般被认为是来源，但它属于通行解释，并非有明文记载的古人说明。

items.en: Greek mys meant both mouse and muscle, showing that the double meaning is very old and not a Latin invention.
items.cn: 希腊语 mys 同时指老鼠与肌肉，说明这种双重含义非常古老，并非拉丁语的独创。

items.en: The ancestor is reconstructed as PIE mus-, seen in several branches of the family; the form is a reconstruction, not an attested word.
items.cn: 其祖词被重构为原始印欧语 mus-，见于语系的多个分支；这一形式是重构形式，并非有书证的词。

items.en: Old French muscle carried the anatomical sense into English in the fourteenth century. The spelling kept the Latin -culus stem but dropped the ending.
items.cn: 古法语 muscle 在 14 世纪把解剖义带入英语。拼写保留了拉丁词干 -culus，但去掉了词尾。

items.en: The division into skeletal, smooth and cardiac muscle belongs to seventeenth- to nineteenth-century physiology; the exact dates of each label are uncertain.
items.cn: 把肌肉分为骨骼肌、平滑肌与心肌，属于 17 至 19 世纪的生理学工作；各名称的准确年代已难确考。

note.en: The first group holds words that look or sound like muscle; the second holds body parts and strength words that are often used in its place.
note.cn: 第一组是与 muscle 形近或音近的词；第二组是常被用来替代它的身体部位词与力量词。

entries.definition: A sea shellfish with a dark shell. It sounds exactly like muscle but has no anatomical meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 一种深色贝壳的海产贝类。读音与 muscle 完全相同，但没有解剖义。

entries.definition: The snout of an animal, or a device fitted over it; the ending is -le after a z sound, not -cle.
entries.definitionCN: 动物的口鼻部，或套在其上的装置；结尾是 z 音后的 -le，而不是 -cle。

entries.definition: The adjective of muscle, meaning relating to muscle or well developed; it cannot replace the noun.
entries.definitionCN: muscle 的形容词，意为「肌肉的」或「肌肉发达的」，不能替代名词。

entries.definition: The whole system of muscles in a body or a region, not one single muscle.
entries.definitionCN: 一个身体或一个部位的全部肌肉系统，而非单独一块肌肉。

entries.definition: A strong cord that attaches muscle to bone; it carries the pull but cannot contract itself.
entries.definitionCN: 把肌肉连到骨的强韧索带；它传递拉力，但自身不能收缩。

entries.definition: A band that holds bone to bone and stabilises a joint; it does not generate movement.
entries.definitionCN: 把骨与骨系住、稳定关节的带状结构；它不产生运动。

entries.definition: An older English word for a tendon, and figuratively for strength; muscle is the flesh that pulls it.
entries.definitionCN: 指肌腱的古老英语词，也可比喻力量；肌肉则是拉动它的那团肉。

entries.definition: Muscular strength, especially of a heavy build; it names the power rather than the organ.
entries.definitionCN: 尤指魁梧体格带来的肌肉力量；它指力量而非器官。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin diminutive, the real Greek double meaning, and real medical compounds.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁指小形式、真实的希腊语双重含义，以及真实的医学术语组合。

normal.en: Latin musculus is a diminutive of mus mouse, and Greek mys has the same double meaning of mouse and muscle.
normal.cn: 拉丁 musculus 是 mus「老鼠」的指小形式，希腊 mys 也有老鼠与肌肉的双重含义。

normal.en: The adjective is muscular and the collective noun is musculature; neither is a plural of muscle.
normal.cn: 形容词是 muscular，集合名词是 musculature；两者都不是 muscle 的复数。

normal.en: Skeletal muscle is voluntary, smooth muscle is involuntary, cardiac muscle is involuntary and rhythmic.
normal.cn: 骨骼肌受意志控制，平滑肌不受控制，心肌不受控制而有节律。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the meanings: muscle mass and muscle fiber are tissue; muscle memory and show muscle are figurative.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分了词义：muscle mass 与 muscle fiber 指组织；muscle memory 与 show muscle 是比喻。

normal.en: The same tissue is called brawn when the point is strength and sinew when the point is the cord.
normal.cn: 当重点在力量时同一组织被称为 brawn，当重点在索带时则称 sinew。

abstract.en: Picture a rope that shortens by itself, and the bone tied to it must follow.
abstract.cn: 想象一根会自己缩短的绳子，被它系住的骨头只能跟着动。

abstract.en: Picture a small animal moving under a cloth: that is the old image behind the Latin name.
abstract.cn: 想象布下有一只小动物在移动：这正是那个拉丁名称背后的古老形象。

abstract.en: Picture influence as a hand pressing on a door: political muscle is the same gesture without a body.
abstract.cn: 想象影响力是一只压住门的手：政治实力就是同一个动作，只是不再有身体。

examples.en: Regular training increases both muscle mass and muscle strength.
examples.cn: 规律训练既能增加肌肉量，也能提高肌力。

examples.en: The diaphragm is a sheet of muscle that drives every breath.
examples.cn: 膈是一层肌肉，驱动每一次呼吸。

examples.en: The company flexed its financial muscle to buy out its rival.
examples.cn: 这家公司展示财力，收购了对手。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马搜」（muscle）——马拉车靠的是一束束能收紧的绳索 → 肌肉

root: 拉丁 musculus「小老鼠」，为 mus「老鼠」的指小形式；一般认为皮下鼓动的肌肉被比作布下跑动的老鼠。希腊语 mys 兼指老鼠与肌肉，祖词为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all rest on one action: fibres shorten and pull. The action is then named as tissue, as a single organ, as three tissue types, as bodily force, as social pressure, as national power, and finally as memory stored in movement.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都建立在一个动作上：纤维缩短并拉动。这个动作依次被命名为组织、单块器官、三种组织类型、身体力量、社会压力、国家实力，最后是储存在动作里的记忆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: bundles of rope that shorten on command and drag whatever they are tied to.
core.cn: 核心意象：一束束听令缩短的绳索，把系住的东西拖着走。

branches.en: MATERIAL AND UNIT: the tissue as material, and one named bundle as an organ.
branches.cn: 材料与单位：作为材料的组织，以及作为器官的一块有名称的肌束。

branches.en: CONTROL TYPES: smooth muscle works unseen, cardiac muscle works without pause.
branches.cn: 控制类型：平滑肌在暗处工作，心肌不停歇地工作。

branches.en: SKILL AND FORCE: strength that moves a piano, and skill that moves without thought.
branches.cn: 力量与技能：能搬动钢琴的力气，以及不经思考就能完成的技能。

branches.en: SHOWN POWER: strength displayed to deter rivals.
branches.cn: 向外展示的力量：为震慑对手而摆出的实力。

branches.en: The bridge between body and politics: the same verb put muscle behind works for both.
branches.cn: 身体与政治的桥梁：同一个搭配 put muscle behind 对两者都适用。

intro.en: Muscle is a Latin diminutive, so its ending -culus is a suffix of smallness rather than a meaningful root; the modern family grows from the stem muscul-.
intro.cn: muscle 是拉丁指小词，结尾 -culus 是表示「小」的后缀而非有实义的词根；现代词族由词干 muscul- 生长出来。

latinIntro.en: Latin musculus and its root mus give the English family muscular, musculature and muscularity; the Greek doublet mys explains why the same image appears in both languages.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 musculus 及其词根 mus 衍生英语的 muscular、musculature、muscularity；希腊语中的对应词 mys 说明两种语言为何出现同一形象。

items.example: The root is the ordinary Latin word for a mouse.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根就是拉丁语中表示老鼠的普通名词。

items.example: Musculus is literally a little mouse.
Latin anatomy named the moving flesh musculus.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁解剖学把会鼓动的肉称为 musculus。

items.example: Muscular tissue responds to nerve signals.
items.exampleCN: 肌肉组织对神经信号作出反应。

items.example: The athlete has a powerful musculature.
items.exampleCN: 这名运动员肌肉系统强健。

items.example: Judges score muscularity as well as leanness.
items.exampleCN: 裁判既看精瘦程度，也看肌肉发达程度。

items.meaning: a heavily built man, often hired as a guard or thug
items.meaningCN: 体格魁梧的男子，常受雇充当打手
items.example: Two musclemen stood at the door.

items.meaning: relating to the link between nerves and muscles
items.meaningCN: 与神经和肌肉连接有关的
items.example: The neuromuscular junction passes the signal across.
items.exampleCN: 神经肌肉接头把信号传递过去。

items.meaning: inside a muscle, as an injection
items.meaningCN: 肌肉内部的，如肌肉注射
items.example: The vaccine was given by an intramuscular injection.
items.exampleCN: 疫苗通过肌肉注射给药。

definition_zh: 博物馆；陈列馆；馆藏机构；专门展室
definition_en: a building where objects of artistic, historical or scientific interest are collected, studied and shown to the public, and also the institution or collection itself
core_image: 玻璃柜里一排旧陶罐，被一盏小灯照出细密的裂纹
scene: 展厅里灯光压得很低，孩子们贴着玻璃柜找一只陶罐上的裂缝，讲解员说它在地下埋了很久。The city museum keeps a whole floor of pottery that was found beneath the old market.
sceneCN: 这里是「博物馆」（第 1 个义项：收藏并陈列文物或艺术品的场所）；句意为这座市立博物馆留出整整一层，陈列旧市场地下挖出的陶器。图中可辨识物件：玻璃柜、陶罐、射灯。

derivatives.zh: 由希腊语 mousa（缪斯）与 -logy（学说）构成，义为「博物馆学」
由 museology 加表示「人」的后缀 -ist 构成，义为「博物馆学专家」
与 museum 同源于缪斯，义为「沉思；冥想」

senses.title: A building that collects and displays objects
senses.definition: a building where objects of art, history or science are collected, kept and shown to the public
senses.definitionCN: 收藏、保存并向公众展示艺术、历史或科学物品的建筑
senses.example: The museum opens at nine and closes at five.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆九点开门，五点闭馆。
senses.why: Greek mouseion was a place of the Muses, a seat of learning, and the modern word still names a building that holds knowledge rather than sells goods.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 mouseion 是缪斯女神的地方，也就是治学之所；现代这个词仍指收藏知识的建筑，而不是卖东西的场所。

senses.title: The institution or collection itself
senses.definition: the institution, or the collection it holds, considered apart from its building
senses.definitionCN: 把这个机构或它收藏的藏品单独来看，而不指建筑本身
senses.example: The museum lent three paintings to a show in another city.
senses.exampleCN: 这家博物馆把三幅画借给了另一座城市的展览。
senses.why: Because the collection travels while the building stays, the name moved from the place to the body that owns and cares for the objects.
senses.whyCN: 藏品可以出借巡展，而建筑留在原地，于是这个名称从「地方」转到「拥有并照管这些藏品」的机构。

senses.title: A room devoted to a special subject
senses.definition: a room or gallery set apart for a particular subject, often smaller than a full museum
senses.definitionCN: 为一个特定主题单独辟出的房间或展廊，通常比完整的博物馆小
senses.example: A small museum of typewriters sits above the bookshop.
senses.exampleCN: 书店楼上有一间小小的打字机陈列室。
senses.why: When the gathering of objects was small and focused, English kept the same word for a single room, so a museum can be a cabinet-sized space for one subject.
senses.whyCN: 当收藏的对象又少又专时，英语仍用同一个词指单个展室，所以 museum 也可以是为一个主题办的小小空间。

intro.en: Museum goes back to the Greek mouseion, a place of the Muses, and it reached English through Latin and French as a name for a place of study.
intro.cn: museum 可追溯到希腊语 mouseion，即缪斯之地；它经拉丁语与法语进入英语，最初指治学之所。

items.en: Mousa, a Muse, named one of the goddesses of poetry, music and learning, and their shrines were places of the arts.
items.cn: mousa 即缪斯，是掌管诗歌、音乐与学问的女神，供奉她们的地方就是艺术之地。

items.en: Mouseion meant a place dedicated to the Muses, a seat of learning where books and objects were kept and discussed.
items.cn: mouseion 意为献给缪斯的地方，是保存并讨论书籍与器物的治学之所。

items.en: Latin borrowed mouseion as museum, keeping the sense of a study or a place of learned pursuits.
items.cn: 拉丁语把 mouseion 借作 museum，仍指书房或治学之所。

items.en: French musée carried the word into the language of galleries, where it named a place holding a collection open to visitors.
items.cn: 法语 musée 把这个词带进画廊的语言，指收藏并向参观者开放的地方。

items.en: Modern English fixes the idea of a public building, and the Greek word for Muse survives inside muse and music.
items.cn: 现代英语把词义固定为公共建筑，希腊语中「缪斯」这个词仍留在 muse 与 music 里面。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the Greek Muse and on the place ending -eum; the near-meaning group collects places and events that hold collections.
note.cn: 形近组收由希腊语「缪斯」与表地点的 -eum 词尾构成的词；近义组收收藏与展示藏品的场所和活动。

entries.definition: To think deeply about something, or a source of inspiration; the word shares the Greek Muse.
entries.definitionCN: 沉思，或灵感的来源；与希腊语缪斯同源。

entries.definition: Sounds arranged to be sung or played; the name comes through the Muses.
entries.definitionCN: 为歌唱或演奏而组织的声音；名称经由缪斯而来。

entries.definition: A picture made of small coloured pieces; the shape is close but the origin differs.
entries.definitionCN: 用小块彩色材料拼成的图画；字形相近，但词源不同。

entries.definition: A large, grand tomb; the ending looks alike but the word comes from a king's name.
entries.definitionCN: 宏伟的陵墓；词尾形似，但这个词来自一位国王的名字。

entries.definition: A room or building where art is shown.
entries.definitionCN: 陈列艺术品的房间或建筑。

entries.definition: A public display of objects or works.
entries.definitionCN: 公开展示物品或作品的活动。

entries.definition: A place or collection of records kept for study.
entries.definitionCN: 为研究保存档案的地方或收藏。

entries.definition: A group of objects gathered and kept together.
entries.definitionCN: 收集并放在一起的一组物品。

normalIntro.en: A Greek place of the Muses became a Latin study, a French gallery and an English public building; the entry follows that journey.
normalIntro.cn: 一个希腊的缪斯之地，先后变成拉丁语的书房、法语的画廊、英语的公共建筑；这个词条就沿着这条路展开。

normal.en: Mouseion was a place of the Muses, so a museum is first of all a home for knowledge, not a shop.
normal.cn: mouseion 是缪斯之地，所以 museum 首先是知识的住所，而不是店铺。

normal.en: The Muses cover poetry and music too, which is why muse and music sit in the same word family.
normal.cn: 缪斯也掌管诗歌与音乐，所以 muse 与 music 留在同一个词族里。

normal.en: -Eum is a place ending borrowed from Greek, so museum, mausoleum and gymnasium share a shape that marks a location.
normal.cn: -eum 是从希腊语借来的地点词尾，所以 museum、mausoleum、gymnasium 共有一个表示场所的形状。

normal.en: English keeps museum for the building, while a gallery can be a single room and a collection can travel.
normal.cn: 英语用 museum 指建筑，而 gallery 可以只是单个房间，collection 则可以出借巡展。

normal.en: Natural history museum joins the word with a subject, which shows the building can be named after what it holds.
normal.cn: natural history museum 把词与一个主题连起来，说明这类建筑可以用所藏之物来命名。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp over a glass case, one cracked pot lit from above.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯照在玻璃柜上，一只裂了缝的陶罐被光从上方照亮。

abstract.en: A place named after goddesses of art suggests that objects are kept so they can be read, not merely stored.
abstract.cn: 一个以艺术女神命名的地方，说明藏品被保存下来是为了供人解读，而不只是堆放。

abstract.en: The word began with study and ended with visitors, so a museum is learning made public.
abstract.cn: 这个词从治学开始，以观众收尾，所以博物馆就是把学问向公众打开。

examples.en: The museum was closed for repairs all summer.
examples.cn: 这座博物馆整个夏天都在维修，暂停开放。

examples.en: We spent a rainy afternoon in the natural history museum.
examples.cn: 下雨的下午，我们待在自然史博物馆里。

examples.en: The museum lent its best painting to a foreign exhibition.
examples.cn: 这家博物馆把最好的一幅画借给了国外的展览。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「缪泽姆」——缪斯女神住的地方，如今成了博物馆；记住 museum。

root: 希腊语 mousa（缪斯）→ mouseion（缪斯之地，治学之所）→ 拉丁语 museum → 法语 musée → 英语 museum；同族词有 muse、music、museology，没有另立的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a place of the Muses; the senses divide into the public building, the institution and its collection, and a single room for one subject.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是缪斯之地；义项分出公共建筑、机构与馆藏，以及为单一主题设的展室。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit glass case holding one cracked pot, with a guide and children in front of it.
core.cn: 核心意象：射灯照着玻璃柜里一只裂陶罐，柜前站着讲解员和孩子。

branches.en: a lit case holding one cracked pot
branches.cn: 射灯照着的一只裂陶罐

branches.en: a crate of paintings sent to another city
branches.cn: 一箱送往另一座城市参展的画

branches.en: a school class walking in behind a guide
branches.cn: 跟着讲解员走进展厅的一个班级

branches.en: a narrow room lined with old typewriters
branches.cn: 摆满旧打字机的狭长展室

branches.en: a name that covers both the walls and the treasures inside them
branches.cn: 一个既指墙壁、也指其中珍藏的名称

intro.en: A Greek noun for the Muses, a Greek place ending and the Latin and English forms built on them hold the entry together.
intro.cn: 一个表示缪斯的希腊名词、一个希腊地点词尾，以及由它们构成的拉丁语与英语形式，撑起了这个词条。

latinIntro.en: Latin passed on the Greek place word as museum, so the Latin forms here are borrowings rather than native relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语把希腊的地点词转写为 museum，所以这里的拉丁形式是借词，而不是本土同族词。

items.meaning: art of sound through the Muses

latinEntries.meaning: a place of study, a library

definition_zh: 蘑菇；菌类；迅速增长；迅速涌现
definition_en: a fungus that grows above ground with a soft stem and a cap, many kinds of which are eaten; also to grow, spread or appear very quickly
core_image: 雨后草地上几朵圆伞般的白菇一夜之间撑开，挤满了整片泥地
scene: 清晨的草地还带着露水，几朵白伞样的菌子从落叶堆里顶出来，比前一天大了整整一圈。Mushrooms appeared across the lawn after two days of rain.
sceneCN: 这里是「蘑菇、菌类」（第 1 个义项：有菌盖与菌柄的肉质真菌）；句意为连下两天雨后，草坪上冒出了一片蘑菇。图中可辨识物件：露水、落叶堆、白色菌盖。

derivatives.zh: 由 mushroom 加 -ing 构成，义为「迅速增多；采蘑菇」
由 mushroom 加表示「人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「采蘑菇的人」

senses.title: A fleshy fungus with a stem and a cap
senses.definition: a fungus that grows above ground with a soft stem and a cap, many kinds of which are eaten
senses.definitionCN: 长在地面、有柔软菌柄与菌盖的真菌，其中许多种类可食用
senses.example: She sliced the mushrooms and added them to the pan.
senses.exampleCN: 她把蘑菇切片放进锅里。
senses.why: The English name probably comes from French mousseron, a word for a kind of mushroom, later reshaped by association with moss where the fungi grow.
senses.whyCN: 英语这个词很可能来自法语 mousseron（一种蘑菇），后来又因为菌子多生于苔藓而被改写成形。

senses.title: Fungi as a group in ordinary use
senses.definition: the group of such fungi, especially the edible kinds sold or gathered as food
senses.definitionCN: 这类真菌的整体，尤指市场上出售或采来食用的种类
senses.example: Wild mushrooms are best kept apart from the rest of the shopping.
senses.exampleCN: 野生蘑菇最好和其余买来的东西分开放。
senses.why: Because cooks and foragers deal with many kinds at once, the same word came to name the category in the kitchen rather than one species.
senses.whyCN: 厨师和采菌人一次面对许多种类，于是同一个词在厨房里成了对整个类别的称呼，而不是某一个物种。

senses.title: To increase very fast
senses.definition: to grow, spread or appear very quickly, like fungi rising overnight
senses.definitionCN: 像菌子一夜冒出那样，迅速地增长、扩散或出现
senses.example: Sales mushroomed after the advertisement ran.
senses.exampleCN: 广告播出之后，销量迅速增长。
senses.why: The picture of a fungus swelling up in a single night supplied a ready metaphor for anything that multiplies suddenly.
senses.whyCN: 菌子在夜里一下子撑开的画面，为任何骤然增多的事物提供了现成的比喻。

intro.en: The name of the mushroom is one of the less certain words in English: it is probably French in origin and was later reshaped by English speakers.
intro.cn: 蘑菇这个词的来源在英语里算不上确定：一般认为出自法语，后来被英语使用者改了形状。

items.en: The earliest forms are hard to trace, and dictionaries mark the origin as uncertain rather than settled.
items.cn: 最早的词形难以追溯，词典把来源标为不确定，而不是已有定论。

items.en: A likely source is French mousseron, a name for a kind of mushroom, which English borrowed and altered.
items.cn: 一般认为来源是法语 mousseron，一种蘑菇的名称，英语借入后改动了拼写。

items.en: English speakers seem to have reshaped the word so that it echoed moss, the damp ground where fungi appear.
items.cn: 英语使用者似乎把这个词改得像 moss（苔藓），也就是菌子常出现的潮湿地表。

items.en: By the sixteenth century mushroom and mushrump were both in use for the edible fungus.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，mushroom 与 mushrump 两种写法都用来指可食用的菌类。

items.en: Modern English fixed the spelling and, from the nineteenth century, extended the word to anything growing with sudden speed.
items.cn: 现代英语固定了拼写，并从十九世纪起把词义扩展到任何迅速增长的事物。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that merely share the shape of mushroom; the near-meaning group collects fungi, their parts and their relatives.
note.cn: 形近组收只是与 mushroom 字形相近的词；近义组收真菌、真菌的构造以及相关词。

entries.definition: Soft, wet pulp, or a command to a team of dogs; only the opening shape resembles this word.
entries.definitionCN: 柔软湿糊的东西，或对拉雪橇犬发出的口令；只是开头形似。

entries.definition: Soft and wet, or excessively sentimental; the shape is close but the word comes from mash.
entries.definitionCN: 又软又湿的，或过分伤感的；字形相近，但这个词来自 mash。

entries.definition: A small green plant that carpets damp ground; it may have influenced the shape of this word, yet it is a different word.
entries.definitionCN: 铺在潮湿地表的小型绿色植物；它可能影响过这个词的写法，但本身是另一个词。

entries.definition: Low wet ground; the spelling and sound are close, the meaning is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 低洼潮湿之地；拼写与读音相近，意义无关。

entries.definition: Any member of the group that includes moulds, yeasts and mushrooms.
entries.definitionCN: 包括霉菌、酵母与蘑菇在内的一类生物。

entries.definition: An umbrella-shaped fungus, especially a poisonous one.
entries.definitionCN: 伞状真菌，尤指有毒的那种。

entries.definition: The reproductive cell of fungi and other simple organisms.
entries.definitionCN: 真菌等简单生物的繁殖细胞。

entries.definition: A soft fungal growth on damp or decaying matter.
entries.definitionCN: 潮湿物或腐败物上长出的真菌。

normalIntro.en: The origin is uncertain, the spelling echoes moss, and the sudden swelling of a fungus gave English a verb for rapid growth.
normalIntro.cn: 来源不确定，拼写又与苔藓相近，而菌子骤然撑开的画面，给英语提供了一个表示迅速增长的动词。

normal.en: The likely French source mousseron already named a mushroom, so the word arrived with its meaning attached.
normal.cn: 一般认为的法语来源 mousseron 本来就指一种蘑菇，所以这个词是带着意思进来的。

normal.en: The modern spelling echoes moss, and mushrooms do rise from damp mossy ground, which makes the link easy to remember even if it is not the true source.
normal.cn: 现代拼写与 moss（苔藓）相近，蘑菇又真从潮湿的苔藓地里冒出来，所以这层联系即使不是真来源也很好记。

normal.en: Mushroom is both noun and verb, so one shape covers the food and the sudden swelling of numbers.
normal.cn: mushroom 既是名词又是动词，一个形状同时管食物和数量的骤增。

normal.en: The plural mushrooms is usual in the kitchen, while the verb takes mushroomed and mushrooming.
normal.cn: 厨房里常用复数 mushrooms，而动词则取 mushroomed 与 mushrooming。

normal.en: Mushroom cloud borrows the cap shape for the plume of an explosion, showing how far the picture travels.
normal.cn: mushroom cloud 借菌盖的形状来形容爆炸的烟柱，可见这个画面能走多远。

abstract.en: Picture white caps pushing through wet leaves overnight, each one a small umbrella.
abstract.cn: 想象一夜之间，白色菌盖顶开湿叶，每一朵都是一把小伞。

abstract.en: A fungus appears without being planted, which is why the word can mean anything that springs up unplanned.
abstract.cn: 菌子没人种也会出现，所以这个词可以指任何不请自来的东西。

abstract.en: The same shape that feeds people also lends its name to explosions, so mushroom carries both growth and blast.
abstract.cn: 同一个形状既养育人，也给爆炸命名，所以 mushroom 同时带着生长与爆裂。

examples.en: He added mushrooms and cream to the soup.
examples.cn: 他往汤里加了蘑菇和奶油。

examples.en: The small business mushroomed into a chain within three years.
examples.cn: 这家小生意三年之内迅速扩张成了连锁店。

examples.en: Some mushrooms in the wood are poisonous and should not be picked.
examples.cn: 林子里有些蘑菇有毒，不该采。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马什鲁姆」——雨后草地一夜撑开一片小伞；记住 mushroom 是蘑菇。

root: 一般认为源自法语 mousseron（一种蘑菇），英语借入后改写，可能受 moss（苔藓）影响；确切来源不确定，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a cap rising from damp ground; the senses divide into the edible fungus, the group of fungi, and sudden rapid growth.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是从潮湿地表顶出的菌盖；义项分出可食用的菌子、菌类整体，以及突然的迅速增长。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: white caps pushing through wet leaves overnight, each one a small umbrella.
core.cn: 核心意象：一夜之间，白色菌盖顶开湿叶，每一朵都是一把小伞。

branches.en: white caps pushing through wet leaves
branches.cn: 湿叶间顶出的白色菌盖

branches.en: a basket holding several kinds of fungi
branches.cn: 装着几种菌子的一只篮子

branches.en: a chart line rising almost straight up
branches.cn: 几乎笔直上升的曲线

branches.en: a crowd forming at a door in minutes
branches.cn: 几分钟内就在门口聚起的人群

branches.en: one shape that feeds a family and also names a blast
branches.cn: 既喂饱一家人、又给爆炸命名的同一个形状

intro.en: A probable French source, a reshaped ending and two English compounds and suffixes carry this uncertain but vivid word.
intro.cn: 一个很可能的法语来源、一个被改写的词尾，以及几个英语复合形式与后缀，撑起了这个来源不确定却画面鲜明的词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded: mushroom is probably of French origin, and the word has no settled Latin relative.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录：mushroom 一般认为出自法语，并没有确定的拉丁亲属词。

items.meaningCN: 来源不确定的改写词尾

items.meaning: cloud shaped like a cap after an explosion

definition_zh: 音乐；乐曲；乐声；配乐
definition_en: sound shaped by rhythm and melody into an art, together with the pieces it produces and the sound heard when it is performed
core_image: 一根琴弓划过琴弦，空气里浮出有秩序的声响
scene: 琴房里没开灯，雨点敲着窗，桌上一本摊开的乐谱被风翻动。The music from the old piano drifted down the empty corridor.
sceneCN: 这里是「音乐」（第 1 个义项：作为声音艺术的音乐）；句意为旧钢琴的乐声沿着空荡的走廊飘远。可辨识物件：钢琴、乐谱、雨中的窗。

derivatives.zh: 由 music 加 -al 构成，义为「音乐的；悦耳的」
由 music 加 -ian 构成，义为「音乐家；乐手」
由 musical 加 -ly 构成，义为「在音乐上；悦耳地」
由 musician 加 -ship 构成，义为「音乐修养；演奏水准」

senses.title: Organized sound treated as an art
senses.definition: sound arranged in rhythm and melody, made by voices or instruments and valued as an art
senses.definitionCN: 按节奏与旋律安排、由人声或乐器发出并被当作艺术的声音
senses.example: She studied music at the conservatory for four years.
senses.exampleCN: 她在音乐学院学了四年音乐。
senses.why: Greek mousike named the work of the Muses, so the word starts as a disciplined craft rather than as any noise that happens to be loud.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 mousikē 原本指缪斯所掌管的技艺，所以这个词的起点是「有章法的技艺」，而不是碰巧很响的杂音。

senses.title: A piece or a body of written works
senses.definition: a particular composition, or the whole set of pieces written by one composer or within one style
senses.definitionCN: 某一首具体的作品，或某位作曲家、某种风格写下的全部作品
senses.example: The orchestra played music by Ravel and Debussy.
senses.exampleCN: 管弦乐队演奏了拉威尔与德彪西的作品。
senses.why: Because one noun can name both the art and the things made by that art, music also points to individual pieces you can put on a programme.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词既能指这门艺术，也能指它做出的东西，因此 music 又可以指可以排进节目单的一首首具体作品。

senses.title: The sound actually heard in performance
senses.definition: the audible sound that reaches the ear when instruments or voices are playing
senses.definitionCN: 乐器或人声演奏时真正传到耳朵里的声音
senses.example: From the next room came the music of a violin.
senses.exampleCN: 隔壁房间传来小提琴的乐声。
senses.why: The abstract art becomes audible only at the moment of playing, so the same noun also names the physical sound filling the room.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的艺术只有在演奏的那一刻才变得可听，于是同一个名词也用来指充满房间的实际声响。

senses.title: Music laid under a film, game or ceremony
senses.definition: music used behind another activity to support its mood or mark its moments
senses.definitionCN: 垫在另一项活动之下、用来烘托气氛或标记节点的音乐
senses.example: The film's music does most of the emotional work.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片的情绪多半由配乐承担。
senses.why: Once music is thought of as a layer under something else, the word takes the role of accompaniment, from cinema to a graduation ceremony.
senses.whyCN: 当音乐被看成垫在别的东西下面的一层，这个词就承担了伴奏的角色，从电影到毕业典礼都是如此。

intro.en: Music reaches English from the Greek art of the Muses by way of Latin and French, and its meaning widened from one craft to works, sound and accompaniment.
intro.cn: music 从希腊语中「缪斯的技艺」出发，经拉丁语与法语进入英语，词义也从一门技艺扩展到作品、声响与伴奏。

items.en: Mousike was the art presided over by the Muses and covered poetry, song and dance rather than instrumental playing alone.
items.cn: mousikē 是缪斯掌管的技艺，包括诗歌、歌唱与舞蹈，并不只指器乐演奏。

items.en: Latin took the word as musica and used it for the art of sound, one of the disciplines of the medieval schools.
items.cn: 拉丁语把这个词写作 musica，用来指声音的艺术，是中世纪学校里的学科之一。

items.en: Old French musique carried the word into everyday use for music and for the notation that records it.
items.cn: 古法语 musique 把这个词带入日常使用，既指音乐，也指记录音乐的谱子。

items.en: Middle English music named both the art and a written score, and the two meanings stayed side by side for centuries.
items.cn: 中古英语的 music 同时指这门艺术和一份写下的乐谱，两个含义并行了数百年。

items.en: Modern English adds the performed sound and the music written for films and ceremonies, so one word covers art, work, sound and setting.
items.cn: 现代英语又加上演奏出来的声响以及为电影、典礼写的配乐，一个词于是覆盖艺术、作品、声音与场景四层。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the forms built on this stem; the near-meaning group collects the things a piece of music is made of.
note.cn: 形近组收由这个词干构成的同族形式；近义组收构成一段音乐的基本元素。

entries.definition: The adjective built on music with -al, meaning of music or sounding pleasant.
entries.definitionCN: 由 music 加 -al 构成的形容词，义为「音乐的」或「悦耳的」。

entries.definition: The person noun built on music with -ian, meaning one who plays or writes music.
entries.definitionCN: 由 music 加 -ian 构成的名词，指演奏或创作音乐的人。

entries.definition: The skill of a musician, formed by adding -ship to musician.
entries.definitionCN: 在 musician 后加 -ship 构成，指音乐家的演奏修养。

entries.definition: The adverb from musical, meaning in a way connected with music.
entries.definitionCN: 由 musical 派生出的副词，义为「在音乐方面」。

entries.definition: The sequence of notes that carries a tune.
entries.definitionCN: 承载曲调的连续音。

entries.definition: A short melody you can hum or whistle.
entries.definitionCN: 可以哼唱或吹出的短曲调。

entries.definition: A piece meant to be sung, words and music together.
entries.definitionCN: 为歌唱而作的作品，词与曲合一。

normalIntro.en: The word is the base of a small family, and the family shows how one noun grows an adjective, a person and a quality.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一小族词的基干，这一族词演示了一个名词如何长出形容词、人物名词和抽象品质。

normal.en: Music is the base of the family: add -al for the adjective musical, add -ian for the person musician.
normal.cn: music 是这一族词的基干：加 -al 得到形容词 musical，加 -ian 得到表示人的 musician。

normal.en: The Greek source mousike meant the art of the Muses, and museum comes from the same shrine, so the two words began as neighbours.
normal.cn: 希腊语 mousikē 意为缪斯的技艺，museum 也出自缪斯的神庙，两个词在源头上是邻居。

normal.en: Music is uncountable, so you say a piece of music or a lot of music, never a music.
normal.cn: music 不可数，所以要说 a piece of music 或 a lot of music，不能说 a music。

normal.en: Sheet music is the written notes rather than the sound, which is why the phrase turns up in every score shop.
normal.cn: sheet music 指纸上写下的音符而不是声响，所以这个说法总出现在卖乐谱的地方。

normal.en: Music to my ears is a fixed idiom for news that makes you glad to hear it.
normal.cn: music to my ears 是固定习语，指让人听了高兴的消息。

abstract.en: Picture the hush in a hall just before the conductor raises a hand: music is what fills that silence on purpose.
abstract.cn: 想象音乐厅里指挥抬手前的那片安静：音乐就是有意填满这片安静的东西。

abstract.en: One noun covering art, works and background sound shows how deeply music is layered into ordinary days.
abstract.cn: 一个名词同时覆盖艺术、作品与背景声音，说明音乐早已层层嵌进平常的日子。

abstract.en: If you can hum it, it is already music, even before anyone writes it down.
abstract.cn: 只要你能把它哼出来，它就已经是音乐，哪怕还没有人把它记下来。

examples.en: She writes music for films and games.
examples.cn: 她为电影和游戏作曲。

examples.en: The music was so loud that we could feel the bass through the floor.
examples.cn: 音乐声太大，隔着地板都能感到低音的震动。

examples.en: He stood listening to the music of a street violinist.
examples.cn: 他站着听一位街头小提琴手的琴声。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「缪齐克」：缪斯女神一抬手，音乐就响了；记住 music 是音乐。

root: 一般认为来自希腊语 mousikē（缪斯的技艺），经拉丁语 musica、古法语 musique 进入英语；同族词围绕「音乐」与「做音乐的人」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is organized sound valued as an art; from it the word reaches the works themselves, the sound heard while playing, and music placed under another activity.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是被当作艺术的有序声音；由此分出具体的作品、演奏时听到的声响，以及垫在别的活动之下的配乐。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bow crossing a string and turning silence into ordered sound.
core.cn: 核心意象：琴弓划过琴弦，把寂静变成有秩序的声响。

branches.en: a practice room where scales slowly become a piece
branches.cn: 琴房里音阶慢慢连成一首曲子

branches.en: a shelf of scores filed under one composer's name
branches.cn: 按一位作曲家名字归档的一架乐谱

branches.en: an orchestra reading a new score for the first time
branches.cn: 乐团第一次读一份新总谱

branches.en: a violin's sound reaching the room next door
branches.cn: 小提琴的声音传到隔壁房间

branches.en: a soundtrack swelling under a closing scene
branches.cn: 片尾画面下渐渐涨起的配乐

intro.en: The family is built on the noun music plus two suffixes: -al for the adjective and -ian for the person, with Latin musica underneath all of them.
intro.cn: 这一族词建立在名词 music 之上，再加 -al 构成形容词、加 -ian 构成指人的名词，底下则是拉丁语 musica。

latinIntro.en: Latin musica came from Greek mousike and became the medieval European word for the art of sound.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 musica 来自希腊语 mousikē，后来成为中世纪欧洲指「声音的艺术」的词。

items.meaning: a person who plays or writes music

latinEntries.meaning: of music, and also a musician
